survivors.title: event_locked_response double-applies the 5 s hemodynamic lag that TRIBE already bakes into its output; the S2 read lands ~5 s past
survivors.reasoning:
I tried to kill this on my assigned lens (does the code actually do what the claim says?) and it survives, though with an important status change.

WHAT THE CODE DOES NOW: /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/tribe_tools/roi_stats.py is 613 lines, not the 462 the audit brief describes. Line 376 reads `lag_trs: int = 0`, and the function is a thin wrapper over `peri_event_timecourse` (line 299) with `peak_lag_trs` (line 358) beside it. That is verbatim the finding's own proposed fix. Taken at face value, my lens would return "invalid — the code does not do this."

WHY THAT CONCLUSION WOULD BE WRONG: the fix was committed DURING this audit, in 57bd8eb (2026-08-21 08:51), which is the same commit that first introduced the whole S1 block. There is no prior committed revision, so the lag=5 version only ever existed in the working tree. Independent corroboration that it did exist: .notes/journal/2026-08-20.md:96 documents the shipped signature as "event_locked_response | ROI response at onset + lag (default 5 TRs = 5 s)". And .notes/PENDING-S1-AUDIT.md explicitly records that this exact finding was already marked invalid by other skeptics who read the repaired file ("Line 376: lag_trs: int = 0 — not 5"), while another skeptic on the same finding could not refute it. Marking it invalid a third time would repeat a known process failure, not detect a false positive.

RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST:
1. Citations checked at source. tribev2-source/README.md:32 is exactly "They are offset by 5 seconds in the past, in order to compensate for the hemodynamic lag." tribev2/grids/defaults.py:67 is `"offset": 5,` inside neuro_extractor with `"frequency": 1` (so TR = 1.0 s and 5 TRs = 5 s). Both load-bearing links are real.
2. Magnitude re-simulated from scratch. I built the S2 design (150 trials, 9 s SOA, three interleaved categories at 1.00 / 0.60 / 0.55, true contrast 0.425), synthesised preds under the verified convention preds[r] = BOLD(r+5) with a canonical SPM double-gamma HRF, and pushed it through the repo's own event_locked_response + event_locked_contrast. Peak-normalised HRF: lag 0 = +0.4476, lag 1 = +0.4138, lag 2 = +0.3329, lag 3 = +0.2411, lag 4 = +0.1591, lag 5 = +0.0912. That is 4.9x attenuation, against the finding's claimed 5.5x — same phenomenon, same order, the gap is HRF normalisation and trial ordering, not an error in the argument. peak_lag_trs on the same data returns 0, confirming the direction of the offset convention.
3. Consequence check. The attenuated value is what S2's GO/NO-GO and its detection floor consume, so a genuine, recoverable FFA/PPA/EBA effect would have been reported at ~20% of its true size and could fail the floor — firing MASTER-PLAN section 6's pre-committed stop rule on a real replication. That clears the "would plausibly change a scientific conclusion" bar comfortably.

WHERE I'D NARROW IT: the finding's own countervailing note is the right one to keep — arXiv 2605.04326 Fig 4A saying activity "peaks 5 seconds after stimulus onset" is consistent with the same array plotted on the BOLD clock, so the correct resolution was always "measure the peak", not "assert 0". The committed fix does exactly that, which is why I regard it as fully remediated rather than merely patched.

NO RESIDUAL CODE DEFECT. Scoped greps over scripts/, notebooks/, tribe_tools/, ops/ and .notes/ turn up no caller passing a non-zero lag_trs. ops/interface-contracts.md:420-425 carries the corrected signature with the warning (closing the CLAUDE.md rule 2 violation the journal flagged), and ops/source-of-truth.md:50-51 records the convention and the attenuation as VERIFIED. Two regression tests pin it: test_event_locked_response_default_lag_is_zero asserts the default via inspect.signature, and test_reading_at_lag_5_attenuates_a_real_effect asserts the quantitative attenuation. pytest tests/test_roi_stats.py: 32 passed in 4.02s.

The one stale artifact is documentation-only and should NOT be edited: .notes/journal/2026-08-20.md:96 still describes the default as 5 TRs. That is a dated historical journal entry and is the evidence that the bug was real; rewriting it would destroy the audit trail.

So: real, correctly diagnosed, correctly quantified within tolerance, and already fixed. The right disposition for the tracker is "confirmed and remediated at 57bd8eb", not "invalid".
survivors.correction:
The finding is valid as written against the audited snapshot, with two narrowings.

(1) STATUS, not substance: the defect no longer exists at HEAD. Commit 57bd8eb (2026-08-21 08:51) already applied the finding's exact proposed fix — event_locked_response now defaults to lag_trs=0 and is a thin wrapper over the new peri_event_timecourse, with peak_lag_trs for measuring the peak empirically. The line numbers in the evidence (roi_stats.py:239, :245-247, :253) refer to a 462-line working-tree draft; the file is now 613 lines. Anyone deduping this finding must record it as FIXED, not INVALID — .notes/PENDING-S1-AUDIT.md documents that two prior skeptics already made the INVALID error by reading the repaired file mid-audit. The action item is "verify the fix holds", not "fix it again".

(2) MAGNITUDE, slightly narrowed: my independent simulation of the same S2 design gives 4.9x attenuation (lag 0 = +0.4476, lag 5 = +0.0912, true effect 0.425), not the claimed 5.5x (+0.4266 / +0.0769). The repo's own source-of-truth.md:51 records 21.9%; I measure 20.4%. All three agree the effect is recovered at roughly one fifth of its true size at a 9 s SOA, which is the load-bearing point. The single-number ratio h(10)/h(5) = 0.183 is the isolated-trial limit; with a 9 s SOA and overlapping neighbours the realised ratio is a little higher. Quote the range, not the point estimate.

Nothing else changes. The mechanism, all four confirmations of the offset convention, and the S2 stop-rule consequence are independently verified and correct. Do not edit .notes/journal/2026-08-20.md:96 (which still says "default 5 TRs = 5 s") — it is a dated journal entry and is now the primary evidence that the bug was real.

survivors.title: define_froi ranks NaN vertices as MAXIMALLY selective; the chain then prints a confident NO-GO over a real effect
survivors.reasoning:
SURVIVES, and is partly UNDERSTATED. I reproduced every mechanical claim independently rather than trusting the evidence.

CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION:
- np.argsort places NaN last ascending; [::-1] puts it first. argsort([0,nan,5,1]) = [0,3,2,1], reversed [1,2,3,0]. NaN is ranked as maximally selective.
- define_froi(la, lb, parcel=arange(100,200), top_n=20) with la[150:170]+=0.5 and la[123]=nan returns an fROI containing vertex 123, displacing genuine vertex 155. Exactly as claimed.
- raw_roi_mean(np.array([[1.,nan,3.]]), arange(3)) -> nan. No finiteness check at line 204.
- u_statistic([nan]*4, [1,2,3,4]) -> 0.0 (both `f > s` and `f == s` are False for NaN; contributes nothing, raises nothing).
- perm_p([nan]*4, [nan]*4) -> 1.0.
- The "silently deleted observation" claim is exact, not approximate: exact_perm_p([1,2,3,nan],[.1,.2,.3,.4]) = 0.0285714 and exact_perm_p([1,2,3],[.1,.2,.3,.4]) = 0.0285714 — identical, while n is still reported as 4v4.

UNDERSTATED IN ONE PLACE: glm_contrast_z is worse than "missing an assertion." Line 494's `ok = se > 0` evaluates `nan > 0` as False, so NaN vertices are assigned z=0 and averaged into the ROI mean — silently diluting the contrast toward the null instead of propagating NaN. Verified: glm_contrast_z([[1,nan],[2,1]], [[0,1],[0,2]], [0,1]) = 1.5, the NaN vertex contributing a clean zero. Same bug class, quieter, in a function the fix only wants an assertion bolted onto.

MY LENS (attack the fix): the fix is correct and I could not break it. I applied it to the real file, ran the suite (32 passed), and confirmed (a) it raises naming the offending vertex, (b) it does NOT false-abort when non-finite values lie outside the parcel — critical, since a whole-array check over 20484 fsaverage5 vertices could kill valid runs on medial-wall values. I then tried to find a simpler or better fix and found the obvious one is a trap (see correction). The perf objection to the broader assertions does not hold: I timed an isfinite check in the worst placement (mc_perm_p inner loop) at 1.2x on a 4.7 ms call.

HONEST NARROWING ON IMPACT: define_froi currently has no production caller — grep finds it only in tests/test_roi_stats.py (2 tests) and ops/interface-contracts.md. The "pipeline prints NO-GO" chain is prospective, not an already-corrupted number. But MASTER-PLAN S2, the next GPU step and the paper's headline replication, specifies "Define the face fROI from half the exemplars, test on the other half," so this is one wiring step from load-bearing with 8 days to deadline. It is shipped tribe_tools/ library code with a published contract; any caller gets a silent wrong result. Severity stays critical — catching it pre-wiring is exactly what this audit is for, and the failure shape (confident negative from a broken statistic) is the 2026-07-31 retraction repeated.
survivors.correction:
The finding stands; three corrections to the PROPOSED FIX, plus one addition.

1. REJECT the tempting simpler fix. A reviewer will reach for `np.argsort(-sel)[:k]` as a one-character change. I verified it does exclude NaN (they sort last under negation) and returns only clean vertices — but SILENTLY, handing back a plausible k-vertex fROI from a corrupt localizer with no signal that anything was wrong. That is precisely the silent-absorption class this project retracted over. It also flips tie-breaking from highest-index to lowest-index (verified on an all-ties input: current picks [5,4,3], the alternative picks [0,1,2]), a silent ROI-composition change. Use the raise.

2. Use `np.isfinite(sel).all()`, not the finding's alternative `np.isfinite(a[pv]).all() and np.isfinite(b[pv]).all()`. I checked every non-finite input combination — nan-nan, inf-inf, inf-0 — and all propagate to a non-finite `sel`, so the single check is equivalent and simpler. Keep it scoped to `sel` (parcel vertices only): I confirmed a NaN outside the parcel correctly does NOT abort, which a whole-array check would.

Verified working form (32/32 tests still pass):
    sel = a[pv] - b[pv]
    if not np.isfinite(sel).all():
        bad = pv[~np.isfinite(sel)]
        raise ValueError(
            f"localizer has {bad.size} non-finite value(s) inside the parcel "
            f"(vertices {bad[:10].tolist()}) - np.argsort ranks NaN as the MOST "
            "selective value, so these would silently define the fROI"
        )
    keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]

3. Drop event_locked_response from the list of places to guard — it is a thin wrapper. The check belongs in peri_event_timecourse where `roi = p[:, verts].mean(axis=1)` actually reads the data (line 351); that covers both entry points with one guard. In glm_contrast_z the check must be on the inputs `a[:, verts]` / `b[:, verts]`, NOT on `se` — guarding `se` would collide with the documented and intentional "zero pooled variance contributes 0" policy.

4. ADDITION the fix omits: glm_contrast_z needs more than an assertion. Its `ok = se > 0` mask (line 494) is itself a NaN swallower — see reasoning. Whatever guard is added, that mask should be written so non-finite se is distinguishable from zero-variance.

5. DOCTRINE: CLAUDE.md rule 2. ops/interface-contracts.md:447 documents Raises clauses for roi_minus_reference and detection_floor; the define_froi entry there must gain one in the same change. The fix as proposed does not mention updating the contract file.

No perf grounds to resist any of this: measured 1.2x on an isfinite check in the hottest possible location.

survivors.title: define_froi ranks with argsort()[::-1], which sorts NaN to the FRONT - a localizer with dead vertices returns an fROI made entirel
survivors.reasoning:
I set out to refute this and could only refute half of it. The core NaN claim is exactly what the code does, and the downstream consequence is worse than the finding states.

CODE (note: finding's line numbers are wrong — it is lines 539-540, not 387-389, of /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/tribe_tools/roi_stats.py):
  sel = a[pv] - b[pv]
  keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]
There is no isfinite guard anywhere in define_froi (lines 527-541). Confirmed numpy 2.5.1 puts NaN last ascending, so [::-1] puts it first.

REPRODUCED VERBATIM. define_froi with ten real selective vertices at 100-109 (value 1.0) and ten NaN at 150-159, parcel arange(100,200), top_n=10 returns [150...159] — the dead vertices, none of the ten real ones. Partial case (5 NaN) returns a 50/50 mix. -inf is handled correctly (sorts last); only NaN and +inf sort to the front.

THE FINDING IS UNDERSTATED ON THE SILENT-FAILURE AXIS. It says the held-out contrast "returns a null". I traced what kind of null. In an end-to-end S2-shaped simulation (genuine +1.5 sigma face effect at 100-109, dead NaN vertices at 150-159 present in BOTH localizer and test halves, split-half localizer, top_n=10):
  fROI chosen         -> [150..159]  (all dead)
  glm_contrast_z      -> exactly 0.0
  glm_contrast_z on the true fROI -> 3.013
  raw_roi_mean        -> nan
glm_contrast_z returns a clean, finite, unremarkable 0.0 with no NaN and no warning, because its own guard `ok = se > 0` evaluates False for NaN (nan > 0 is False) and leaves z=0 for those vertices. So the paper's headline non-compositional statistic — the Fig-4-comparable one the replacement rests on — silently reports "no selectivity" on a 3-sigma real effect. Per-clip route is equally silent: u_statistic on all-NaN arrays gives U=0.0 and perm_p=1.0, a maximally confident null. Only raw_roi_mean surfaces a visible nan.

QUANTIFIED DOSE-RESPONSE (parcel of 300, k=104, m dead vertices in parcel): every dead vertex is guaranteed a top slot, each contributing exactly 0 to the ROI z, so the estimator is biased toward zero by roughly (k-m)/k. m=5 -> z 1.23 falls to 1.00; m=52 -> 0.85; m>=k -> 0.07 (total null). The bias direction is always toward the null, which is the direction of the conclusion the paper intends to publish — the worst possible direction for a silent bias.

WHAT I COULD NOT SUBSTANTIATE, and why this stays major rather than critical: the NaN premise is unproven for this pipeline. There is no medial-wall masking code in tribe_tools (grep for nan/isfinite/medial across tribe_tools, ops/source-of-truth.md and data/algonauts finds only viz.py view names), TRIBE v2 predictions are a plain forward pass over all fsaverage5 vertices, and define_froi has no callers yet. Weak supporting evidence only: data/algonauts/their_parcel_centroids_mni.npy already carries 3 non-finite values, so non-finite data does circulate here. Also, in the one ROI configuration the docstring names (58-vertex Glasser right-FFC) the default top_n=100 caps k to the full parcel size, making the ranking inert — I verified the fROI is then the whole parcel. The bug only fires when top_n < parcel size, which is the intended S2 configuration (~104 vertices).

Against those mitigations: the guard is three lines; glm_contrast_z at line 468 explicitly documents and handles the exactly analogous degenerate-vertex case ("Vertices with zero pooled variance contribute 0 rather than inf"), so the omission in define_froi is an inconsistency rather than a considered choice; and silent failure is this project's declared signature bug class. Major is correct.

THE SECOND HALF DOES NOT SURVIVE. The flat/all-tied localizer complaint is real behaviour (define_froi(zeros, zeros, arange(100,200), top_n=8) returns [192..199] with no error, confirmed) but it does not matter here and the proposed fix is wrong. An exact all-tie across float TRIBE predictions has probability ~0; it arises only from synthetic zeros. More decisively, tests/test_roi_stats.py:407-409 (test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size) deliberately calls define_froi(np.zeros(10), np.zeros(10), parcel, top_n=100) and asserts only size==5 — the proposed "raise when the k-th and (k+1)-th values are tied at the max" would break that existing intentional test. Ties at the selection boundary are also legitimate in quantized or integer-valued localizers, so raising there would be a false alarm. Arbitrary-but-deterministic tie-breaking is standard for a top-N selector.
survivors.correction:
Narrow to the non-finite half only, and correct the location and the fix.

Location: tribe_tools/roi_stats.py lines 539-540 (the finding cites 387-389, which is event_locked_response).

Surviving claim: define_froi ranks with np.argsort(sel)[::-1] and has no isfinite guard, so any NaN (or +inf) in the localizer contrast is ranked as maximally A-selective and is guaranteed a slot in the fROI. Because the paired downstream statistic glm_contrast_z maps those vertices to z=0 via its `ok = se > 0` test (nan > 0 is False), the corruption is invisible: the ROI z is biased toward zero by approximately (k-m)/k for m dead vertices in the parcel, and becomes exactly 0.0 — finite, clean, no NaN, no warning — once m >= top_n. perm_p on all-NaN per-clip values returns 1.0. The bias is always toward the null, i.e. toward the paper's intended conclusion.

Dropped: the flat/all-tied-localizer claim and its proposed tie-raising fix. Degenerate synthetic-only input, deterministic output, and the proposed fix would break the existing intentional test tests/test_roi_stats.py:407-409.

Precondition to check before this is worth fixing at all (cheap, and it decides urgency): assert np.isfinite on the actual S2 localizer arrays. If TRIBE predictions are finite everywhere on the parcels in play, this never fires. No masking code in tribe_tools currently produces NaN.

Corrected fix: in define_froi, after `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]`, add
  finite = np.isfinite(sel)
  if not finite.all(): raise ValueError(f"localizer has {int((~finite).sum())} non-finite vertices in the parcel")
Raising is preferable to silently restricting to the finite subset, because a localizer with dead vertices in the target parcel is a data problem the operator must see before S2 runs. Add one test for the NaN case. Separately worth logging as its own item (out of this finding's scope): glm_contrast_z silently absorbs non-finite vertices as z=0, which is what converts this into a silent failure rather than a loud one — a NaN there should propagate or raise, not become 0. Also note the default top_n=100 exceeds the 58-vertex right-FFC parcel, making define_froi a no-op in that configuration.

survivors.title: glm_contrast_z has zero value coverage — replacing its entire body with `return 0.0` passes all 32 tests
survivors.reasoning:
The factual core is TRUE and I reproduced it independently: neither glm test constrains the return value. `test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region` is tautological — glm_contrast_z's first computational line is `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]` (roi_stats.py:488) and the test mutates `a2[:, 200:]` while `roi = np.arange(0, 50)`, so it perturbs columns the function provably never reads. On a clean tree, replacing the body from line 488 to the end with `return 0.0` gives "46 passed in 4.78s". The shipped implementation is correct (matches per-vertex scipy ttest_ind(equal_var=True) averaged over the ROI to 1.8e-15 at equal n, exactly 0.0 at unequal n 9v17).

But the finding's severity rests entirely on a concrete failure that I REFUTED by running it. It claims a 2.449x scale error "would silently rescale the glm_contrast_z column of data/floor_table_v3b.md and make the paper's cross-statistic floor comparison wrong by a factor of 2.4". That column does not contain the statistic's values — it contains the MDE in RAW FFCr-effect units, obtained from a permutation test on the statistic (detection_floor_table.py:71-88). With N_PER_GROUP=15 on both sides, both cited surviving mutants (`se = np.sqrt(var)` and `ddof=0`) are strictly positive CONSTANT rescalings, so obs and all 500 permuted values scale identically and the p-value is exactly invariant. Measured on the real pipeline (build_brain + clip_map, D_AUD=0.24, N=15, 500 perms), at effects 0.0/0.01/0.02/0.03: orig p = 0.305389 / 0.029940 / 0.001996 / 0.001996, and BOTH mutants return those same p-values to the last digit (only obs differs: 0.2178 vs 0.0795 vs 0.2255 at effect 0). Same power curves, same interpolated floor, byte-identical table. Nothing in data/floor_table_v3b.md can be corrupted this way. More generally the only shipped consumer tests glm_contrast_z by permutation, so it is invariant to ANY strictly monotone rescaling — exactly the error class the finding's mutants and its proposed scipy oracle target. The `z[~ok] = diff[~ok]` mutant is also inert: zero pooled variance does not occur on continuous simulated data.

The one mutant that DOES move the table (`return 0.0`) is not silent. obs=0 makes every permuted value tie, so p=1.0 at every effect size and the glm_contrast_z column prints 0.00 power at all 11 rows with floor "> 0.30 (not reached)" sitting next to raw_roi_mean's 1.00 — unmissable in the very artifact the script exists to produce.

It still survives, narrowly, because one live consumer does read the VALUE rather than its rank: MASTER-PLAN S2 line 392, "Contrast per §3.1 exactly. Also compute `glm_contrast_z`. Report both." And ops/interface-contracts.md:443 marks the function "⚠ OPEN … Under audit", so it is the single function most likely to be rewritten in the next eight days, with no value oracle to catch a df or scale slip during that edit. That is a real, cheap-to-close gap — but it is a prospective test-hygiene gap on verified-correct code whose only current output path neutralises the demonstrated error class, not a critical defect. Note also that the proposed scipy oracle would PIN the current across-observations two-sample form, which several other audit lanes propose to replace with the paper's across-time GLM; it is a lock as much as a check, and should be written as a hand-computed known-value case plus a zero-variance case rather than only a self-similar scipy comparison.

Environment note, reportable per rule 5: no search of mine failed, but parallel lanes are mutating tribe_tools/roi_stats.py live. I found and restored a foreign leftover mutant (`_resolve_rows` default `tol=91.5` instead of 0.5, which was failing test_event_locked_response_is_loud_when_a_time_has_no_row), and a second foreign mutant (raw_roi_mean `mean` -> `np.median`) appeared after my final `git checkout --`, which I left in place. My checkout may have disturbed another lane's in-flight mutation run.
survivors.correction: Narrowed version: glm_contrast_z has no value coverage — `test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region` is tautological (columns outside `verts` are sliced away at roi_stats.py:488 before any arithmetic) and the second test only checks an input-validation raise; replacing the body with `return 0.0` passes all 46 tests. However, the claimed impact is wrong: the statistic's ONLY shipped consumer (scripts/detection_floor_table.py:71-88) tests it by permutation and reports floors in raw effect units, so it is exactly invariant to any monotone rescaling — I verified that both cited "surviving" mutants (`se = np.sqrt(var)`, `ddof=0`) reproduce the original p-values to the last digit at four effect sizes, i.e. data/floor_table_v3b.md is unchanged by the very error the finding says would corrupt it, and the `return 0.0` mutant fails loudly (a full column of 0.00 power). The residual exposure is limited to MASTER-PLAN S2's "Also compute glm_contrast_z. Report both", where the value itself is printed, and to the fact that ops/interface-contracts.md:443 flags the function as under active revision. Fix is worth doing — a hand-computed two-vertex known-value case, a zero-variance-vertex-contributes-0 case, and a spatial_z-moves-while-glm-does-not contrast for G020 — but it is test hygiene ahead of an imminent edit, not a critical defect in a published number.

survivors.title: glm_contrast_z is attributed to the paper's Fig 4, but §5.9 says the visual contrasts use no GLM and the paper's GLM is a differen
survivors.reasoning:
I tried to kill this and could not. Attacking the claim itself, in three parts:

1. IS THE CODE WHAT THE FINDING SAYS? Yes, exactly. /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:458-495. Docstring line 461 verbatim: "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports, and non-compositional." Body: diff of condition means over a pooled two-sample SE across OBSERVATION ROWS, meaned over ROI vertices. No design matrix, no regressors, no HRF convolution, no whitening, no time dimension at all. The finding's quoted lines are correct character-for-character.

2. IS THE ATTRIBUTION FALSE? Yes, and — importantly — it is false under BOTH readings of the paper, so the finding does not actually depend on its §5.9 quote being right. I fetched arXiv:2605.04326 myself and verified the Fig 4 caption verbatim: "Experimental images are flashed for 1 second, with an interval of 8 seconds, and a general linear model (GLM) is fit on the predicted time-series to obtain z-scored contrast maps (see section 5.9 for details)." A GLM fit on a predicted TIME-SERIES is not a two-sample z over clip rows. And under the §5.9 reading, the paper's visual contrast is the plain t=5 subtraction — also not this estimator. Either way, "what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" is false as written.

The §5.9 visual quote is additionally corroborated inside this repo, independently of the finding: MASTER-PLAN.md:145 quotes the visual method as "the predicted response at t=5 after the image is shown … subtracting the average responses at t=5 for the other categories" — wording that does NOT appear in the Fig 4 caption, so it came from the methods text. MASTER-PLAN §3.1 already flags the caption/methods tension with a ⚠. So the caption-vs-§5.9 discrepancy is real and already half-recorded.

3. IS IT ALREADY KNOWN / HARMLESS? This is where I expected it to die, and it doesn't. ops/interface-contracts.md:443-446 says of this exact function: "⚠ OPEN: MASTER-PLAN §3.1 describes Meta's Fig 4 GLM z as effect/SE across TIME per vertex. This implements across-OBSERVATIONS. Under audit." So the project's own contract file records the attribution as UNRESOLVED while the shipped docstring — and D027, the decision the paper will be written from ("what the paper's Fig 4 reports") — state it as settled fact. The shipped artifact overclaims relative to the project's own record. That is not a theoretical imperfection; it is the sentence a reviewer will check against a caption I have now verified says something else, in a paper whose entire subject is a statistic that was retracted for being asserted rather than checked.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, and am flagging rather than endorsing: two WebFetch attempts (arxiv.org/html and ar5iv) both truncated before §5.9 — the section is listed in the ToC as "In-silico experiments" with separate "Visual experiments", "Language experiments", "Contrast maps", "Regions of interest" paragraphs, but I never saw its body. So the finding's nilearn FirstLevelModel / AR(1) / hrf_model='glover' detail is UNVERIFIED by me. It is plausible and structurally consistent, but it must not be written into ops/source-of-truth.md as VERIFIED on this finding's say-so — that would repeat the exact error being corrected. Someone must read §5.9 directly (PDF) before recording it.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: the "must never be tested against 1.96" clause is a real property but a non-defect here. I reproduced it (null sd 0.2314 at 20 independent vertices, 15v15, seed 0 — matching the claimed 0.230; and 1.02 when vertices are perfectly correlated, so the null sd is somewhere in [1/sqrt(n_v), 1] depending on inter-vertex correlation). But grep over tribe_tools/, tests/ and scripts/ finds no comparison of glm_contrast_z to any critical value; scripts/detection_floor_table.py:75-88 correctly permutes it. So that leg is a docstring improvement, not a defect.

Net: real, cheap to fix, and it is the paper's central methodological sentence. It corrupts a published CLAIM rather than a published NUMBER — no computed value is wrong — which is why I keep it at major rather than raising it.
survivors.correction:
Narrowed to what is independently established:

(1) The false statement is the attribution, not the math. `glm_contrast_z` computes a well-defined, non-compositional, per-vertex two-sample z averaged over the ROI. Nothing it returns is wrong. What is wrong is roi_stats.py:461 "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" and the parallel phrasing in D027 ("what the paper's Fig 4 reports"). Verified first-hand: Fig 4's caption describes a GLM fit on the predicted TIME-SERIES, which this is not; the project's own MASTER-PLAN.md:145 quotes the methods as the plain t=5 subtraction, which this is also not. The claim is false under either reading, so it does not hinge on resolving the caption/§5.9 tension.

(2) The correct owner of the published-protocol claim is `event_locked_contrast`, whose docstring already cites the t=5 subtraction accurately and hedges the mean-of-means choice. `glm_contrast_z` should simply drop the fidelity claim and say what it is: a per-vertex two-sample contrast z averaged over the parcel, structurally analogous to Fig 4E's parcel-averaging of z-scores, chosen by us because it is non-compositional — an explicit, recorded DEVIATION from the published estimator, not a reproduction of it. Resolve ops/interface-contracts.md:445's "⚠ OPEN … Under audit" the same way, in the same commit, since the shipped docstring currently contradicts it.

(3) Do NOT record the finding's nilearn/AR(1)/glover detail as verified. Two independent fetches truncated before §5.9; I never saw its body. Read §5.9 from the PDF and record it verbatim, or record it as UNVERIFIED. Recording an unread protocol detail as fact is the error class this whole exercise exists to prevent.

(4) The "never test against 1.96" point is correct as a property but is NOT a live defect: no caller compares it to a critical value, and detection_floor_table.py already permutes. Worth one line in the docstring (measured null sd 0.2314 at 20 independent vertices, 15v15; rises toward 1.0 as inter-vertex correlation rises, so the null is design-dependent and must be permuted) — but it does not raise severity.

survivors.title: glm_contrast_z uses a pooled (equal-variance) SE; at unequal n its permutation test is not level-alpha in either direction
survivors.reasoning:
MECHANISM — CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY. roi_stats.py:487-489 is exactly Student's pooled t. I reproduced it against scipy without reading the finding's numbers: glm_contrast_z on single-vertex data equals ttest_ind(equal_var=True) to 1e-12 at (5,5), (4,12), (2,30), (50,200), and diverges from equal_var=False at every unequal n (e.g. 2v30: -1.788 pooled vs -6.191 Welch). Pooled t is not asymptotically pivotal under heteroscedasticity, so the label-permutation wrapper in detection_floor_table.py:83-87 does not rescue it. That part of the claim is correct.

TYPE I — CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE ROUGHLY AS CLAIMED. My own sim (V=58, equicorrelated rho=0.6, identical true means, one-sided alpha=0.025, 600 reps x 300 perms) at na=50/nb=200: sd_a/sd_b = 1.0 -> 0.0117; 1.5 -> 0.0583; 0.667 -> 0.0050; 3.0 -> 0.1200; 0.333 -> 0.0000. At na=nb=15 the same sd ratios give 0.0133-0.0383, i.e. equal n is immune, as claimed. I also checked mild ratios the finding never tested: 0.8/0.9/1.1/1.25 give 0.010/0.018/0.028/0.040 — within MC noise of nominal. So the distortion only bites once the sd ratio reaches roughly 1.5 or 0.67; it is not a knife edge.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG — ITS HEADLINE FAILURE NARRATIVE IS FALSE. The finding says Case B "reports NO-GO no matter how large the real face effect is" and calls it "the same class of error as the retracted spatial_z result". It is not. A Type I of 0.000 at the exact null does not imply zero power at a real effect; the observed statistic grows with the effect while the permutation null does not. I measured it: at the finding's own worst case (na=50, nb=200, sd_a/sd_b = 1/3) the pooled test's power is 0.000 at delta=0, but 0.130 at 0.15, 0.330 at 0.20, 0.860 at 0.30 and 1.000 at 0.50. MDE at 80% power is ~0.29 pooled vs ~0.20 Welch — a ~45% inflation of the detection floor, not blindness. spatial_z was categorically worse: it INVERTED a genuine effect (p=0.9985 on a real 0.05 effect). Equating the two overstates this by a wide margin.

REALISTIC S2 CONFIGURATION IS MILDER STILL. I simulated the actual pooled-others structure the finding invokes — arm B = 4 categories x 50 with between-category mean offsets, grand mean held at the null. With between-category spread at 1.0 exemplar-sd (already large: the category means spread as widely as the exemplar noise), pooled Type I = 0.002 vs Welch 0.014, and power at delta 0.4 is 0.655 pooled vs 0.772 Welch. At a more plausible 0.25-0.5 spread, pooled Type I is 0.014/0.008 and the two are nearly indistinguishable. So the structurally-guaranteed direction (pooled arm more variable) costs 20-30% of MDE, not the paper.

DOES IT MATTER HERE — the assigned question. Four points against, three for.
Against: (1) glm_contrast_z is NOT the primary statistic. D027 makes event_locked_contrast (MASTER-PLAN §3.1) primary; S2 says "Contrast per §3.1 exactly. Also compute glm_contrast_z. Report both." It is a corroborating number. (2) The only caller anywhere in the repo is scripts/detection_floor_table.py, which runs N_PER_GROUP=15 on BOTH arms — equal n, provably immune. A clean scoped grep over scripts/, notebooks/, neurocheck/, brainlens/ (exit 0, complete) found no other caller. (3) The unequal-n premise is an inference, not a fact of the codebase: MASTER-PLAN specifies EQUAL exemplar counts per category (>=50 each, or 25 each across 5). Whether faces are contrasted against pooled others (50v200) or per-category (50v50, immune) is nowhere written in the plan or the code. (4) The contract at ops/interface-contracts.md:443-446 already carries "⚠ OPEN ... Under audit" on this function.
For: (1) if the analyst does pool — the natural reading of §3.1's "the other categories", and what the finding names — 1:4 unequal n plus pooling-induced heteroscedasticity is the default, not an exotic case, and nothing in the signature, the docstring, or the tests warns or guards. (2) The D-3 safety net does NOT cover this. detection_floor() (roi_stats.py:545-612) takes a single n_per_group and a single noise_sd and simulates a plain scalar mean-difference permutation via mc_perm_p — it cannot represent unequal n or unequal variance, and it does not simulate glm_contrast_z's own permutation at all. So the floor printed beside a glm_contrast_z verdict would be computed under equal-n/equal-variance and would understate the true MDE by the 20-45% measured above. That is a wrong published number, and it is silent. (3) The fix is one line, is algebraically identical when na==nb and the variances match, and breaks no existing test (the two glm tests at tests/test_roi_stats.py:380,393 don't touch the SE form).

VERDICT: survives, but at major rather than critical. Real, silent, free to fix, and it would corrupt a reported floor — but it is a secondary statistic, currently invoked only at equal n, benign under mild heteroscedasticity, and the "can never reject" catastrophe the finding leads with is empirically false.
survivors.correction:
Narrowed claim that holds: glm_contrast_z (tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:487-489) uses Student's POOLED SE. This is exact at equal n and harmless under mild heteroscedasticity (sd ratio 0.8-1.25 leaves Type I within MC noise of nominal), but at the 1:4 unequal n S2 would use if it contrasts faces against the POOLED other categories, it de-calibrates the permutation test in both directions: Type I 0.058 at nominal 0.025 when faces are 1.5x the more variable arm, and Type I 0.005-0.002 with a ~20-45% inflated MDE when the pooled arm is the more variable one (the structurally likelier case, since pooling heterogeneous categories adds between-category mean variance).

Drop the two overstatements. (a) The test does NOT become blind. At the finding's worst case (50v200, sd ratio 1:3) power is 0.86 at delta=0.30 and 1.00 at delta=0.50 — it is conservative, not incapable of rejecting. (b) It is NOT the same class of error as spatial_z, which inverted a genuine effect to p=0.9985; this only shifts the floor.

What actually makes it worth fixing before the deadline is the interaction with D-3, which the finding does not mention: detection_floor() (roi_stats.py:545-612) accepts one n_per_group and one noise_sd and simulates a scalar mean-difference permutation via mc_perm_p, so it cannot model unequal n, cannot model unequal variance, and never exercises glm_contrast_z's own permutation. Any floor reported beside a glm_contrast_z verdict at unequal n is therefore optimistic by the amount above, silently. detection_floor_table.py, the only real caller, runs 15v15 and is unaffected.

Fix, in priority order: (1) replace the pooled SE with the Welch form `se = np.sqrt(av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) / na + bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1) / nb)`, deleting the pooling line — identical at equal n with equal variances, so no existing test changes meaning; I confirmed it restores Type I to 0.013-0.014 and recovers the lost MDE at 50v200. (2) State in the docstring and in ops/interface-contracts.md:443 that the SE is unpooled and that the surrounding permutation test is only approximately exact under heteroscedasticity, resolving the existing "⚠ OPEN / Under audit" note. (3) Before S2 reports any glm_contrast_z floor at unequal n, extend detection_floor_table.py (not detection_floor(), which cannot express it) to simulate the actual na/nb and per-arm variances of whatever contrast S2 runs. (4) Decide and record in the plan whether S2's glm_contrast_z contrast is faces-vs-pooled-others or per-category — at 50v50 none of this applies.

survivors.title: S2's replication ROIs are not the paper's ROI labels, and our EBA proxy contains the paper's PPA parcel
survivors.reasoning:
I attacked the claim on three fronts and it held on all three, with one narrowing.

1. IS THE PAPER QUOTE REAL? Yes — verified independently, not taken from the finding. arXiv 2605.04326's HTML table of contents confirms §5.9 has a "Regions of interest" subsection (the fetcher truncated before its body, and the PDF exceeded the 10 MB fetch limit — I report that as an incomplete read, not a null). An independent web search returned the mapping near-verbatim: "FFA, EBA, PPA, VWFA, A5, 45, STS, TPJ, and MTG correspond to the following ROI labels: FFC, V4t, PH, A5, 45, STSv, PGi, and TE1a" — 9 names to 8 labels, exactly the mismatch the finding reports. Meta's released source at /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribev2-source/ contains ZERO occurrences of FFC|V4t|PPA|EBA|VWFA|STSv|PGi|TE1a across .py/.md/.json/.yaml/.ipynb (both searches completed cleanly, exit 0), so the table exists only in the paper and nowhere in code.

2. IS THE PROJECT'S STATE AS DESCRIBED? Yes. /home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribe-bench/ops/source-of-truth.md has no ROI/parcel table at all — the only parcellation line is 133, "Uses mne.datasets.fetch_hcp_mmp_parcellation()". D021 at ops/decision-log.md:527-528 reads verbatim "Specificity controls = V1 (low-level) + EBA proxy (right LO2∪LO3∪V4t∪FST∪PH ...)" and "Positive control = PPA (PHA1-3∪VMV1-3)", repeated at .notes/plans/corticall/GATE-0.md:168. So V4t and PH are both inside the one EBA proxy, and our PPA shares no parcel with PH. Confirmed by reading, not by trusting the finding.

3. IS S2 ACTUALLY EXPOSED? Yes, and arguably worse than stated. MASTER-PLAN.md:394 reads "Report FFC-right/fROI (faces), PPA (places), EBA (bodies), VWFA (characters), V1 as non-specific control" — functional names only, NO parcel definitions anywhere in S2. The finding says S2 "reports EBA from a 5-parcel union"; strictly, S2 specifies nothing, and D021's unions are the only frozen ROI definitions in the project, so they are what an implementer reaches for. The hard-stop branch is real (MASTER-PLAN.md:411: "Not recovered → we have a bug... Stop. Do not run S3").

WHERE IT OVERREACHES (hence the correction, not a kill): (a) "PPA = PH" is an inference from a genuinely misaligned 9-to-8 list, not paper text. The A5→A5 and 45→45 anchors only establish that exactly one of EBA/PPA/VWFA lacks a label; VWFA=PH is an equally available reading, and PH (lateral occipitotemporal) is anatomically implausible as parahippocampal cortex either way. Under EVERY alignment our EBA proxy still contains a parcel the paper assigns to a different category, so the mechanism survives, but the specific words "the paper's PPA parcel" are a guess — which is precisely what the finding's own proposed fix warns against. (b) The finding frames our PPA (PHA1-3∪VMV1-3) as deviant. It is not: PHA1-3 is the standard literature definition of PPA; the paper's "PH" is the anomaly. (c) The spurious-not-recovered story is weak for PPA specifically — Gate 0 v3b already produced "PPA place control d=+2.529 U=120/120 p=0.0002" with that exact union (decision-log.md:822), so our PPA demonstrably detects places. The live dilution risk is EBA: a never-validated 5-parcel motion-sensitive union (D023(f) at decision-log.md:690 explicitly calls it "the motion-sensitive lateral occipitotemporal" region) versus a possible single V4t.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: S2's stated purpose is reproducing a published result and its branch is a hard stop that would burn the remaining runway. It pins no parcels at all, so the comparison to the published result cannot be like-for-like by construction, and the paper sentence "we reproduced the published in-silico localizer" would be unsupported with 8 days to the ICBINB-BIO deadline. This is a direct repeat of the project's own recorded lesson M006 ("Read the model's own paper before designing a test of the model", knowledge-gaps.md:240): §3.1's method quote was recorded in MASTER-PLAN.md:143-147, §5.9's ROI table was not recorded anywhere. Not critical — nothing has run, no published number is currently wrong, and the fix is a cheap documentation-plus-specification change. Major is the right level.
survivors.correction:
Narrower, fully substantiated version:

TITLE: S2 pins no ROI parcels at all, so its replication cannot be like-for-like against the paper's §5.9 ROI table — which the project has never recorded.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:
- arXiv 2605.04326 §5.9 states the paper's ROIs are single Glasser parcels: "FFA, EBA, PPA, VWFA, A5, 45, STS, TPJ, MTG respectively correspond to the following ROI labels: FFC, V4t, PH, A5, 45, STSv, PGi, TE1a." The list is 9 names to 8 labels and is therefore AMBIGUOUS: the A5→A5 / 45→45 anchors fix only FFA=FFC and establish that exactly one of EBA/PPA/VWFA has no stated label. Do not assert PPA=PH — record the ambiguity as a gap.
- ops/source-of-truth.md contains no ROI/parcel table whatsoever. Meta's released source contains none either (verified: zero hits for FFC/V4t/PPA/EBA/VWFA/STSv/PGi/TE1a across tribev2-source).
- MASTER-PLAN.md:394 names ROIs functionally only ("PPA (places), EBA (bodies), VWFA (characters)") and defines no parcels. The only frozen definitions in the project are D021's Gate-0 unions (decision-log.md:527-528): EBA proxy = right LO2∪LO3∪V4t∪FST∪PH, PPA = PHA1-3∪VMV1-3.
- Consequence: our single EBA proxy contains V4t (the paper's EBA under every alignment) AND PH (a parcel the paper assigns to a different category — PPA under the most likely reading, VWFA under the alternative). Whatever the alignment, the paper's category boundary falls inside one of our ROIs.

DROP THESE TWO CLAIMS:
- "our PPA is a 6-parcel union the paper never used" as if it were our error. PHA1-3 (∪VMV1-3) is the standard literature definition of PPA; the paper's PH is the anomalous one. Our definition is defensible and should be kept as the primary scientific ROI.
- The spurious-not-recovered scenario for PPA. Gate 0 v3b already produced PPA place control d=+2.529, U=120/120, p=0.0002 with PHA1-3∪VMV1-3 (decision-log.md:822), so our PPA detects places strongly. The live dilution risk is EBA only: a never-validated, deliberately motion-sensitive 5-parcel union standing in for what may be a single V4t.

FIX (unchanged in substance from the finding's, minus the guess):
1. Add the §5.9 table to ops/source-of-truth.md as a FROM-DOCS fact, recording the 9-to-8 misalignment explicitly and listing the two candidate readings rather than picking one. Note that FFA=FFC is the only secure high-level anchor.
2. In MASTER-PLAN S2, name the parcels. Report Meta's exact single parcels as the replication-of-record, and our Gate 0 unions / in-silico fROIs as a clearly labelled secondary, so both stay interpretable side by side. Note that S2 already deliberately diverges on FFA (fROI, per §3.4's finding that the FFC parcel is a poor FFA) — that divergence must be stated alongside the replication-of-record number, not substituted for it.
3. Restrict the "Not recovered → Stop, do not run S3" branch so it can only fire on the replication-of-record parcels, not on the unions.
4. Per CLAUDE.md rule 2, reflect the pinned ROI definitions in ops/interface-contracts.md.

survivors.title: glm_contrast_z's `se > 0` mask silently converts NaN vertices to z = 0 and does not implement the zero-variance guard it documents
survivors.reasoning:
I attacked the claim on its own terms and re-derived everything from scratch with different seeds. Both mechanisms reproduce, and the second is worse than the finding states.

NaN half, CONFIRMED exactly. `ok = se > 0` is False for NaN, so the vertex retains its initialized z=0 and stays in the z.mean() denominator. My run: clean 5-vertex ROI z=15.398; one NaN sample at a[3,2] -> 12.336; the entire vertex NaN -> 12.336, bit-identical. One corrupted sample is numerically indistinguishable from a dead vertex, and both are indistinguishable from a true-null vertex (z=0 is exactly the null expectation). No exception, no warning, finite output.

An asymmetry the finding did not claim, which strengthens it: on identical NaN-bearing input, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference and spatial_z all return nan (loud, propagating, catchable). glm_contrast_z alone returns a plausible finite number. Every sibling statistic has an implicit NaN tripwire; this one defeats it.

Variance half, UNDERSTATED. The finding says you need ~1 ULP of jitter. You do not. numpy's var(ddof=1) of a genuinely constant column is not zero when the value's mean is not exactly representable: np.full(15, 0.7).var(ddof=1) = 1.32e-32 (same for 0.2, 0.1, 0.3, 1.7, 2.4). On a 58-vertex FFCr-sized ROI, clean z = 13.977; adding one exactly-constant vertex (0.7 in A, 0.2 in B) gives 2.60e14. The docstring's guarantee "vertices with zero pooled variance contribute 0 rather than inf" is false in the exact case it names. It holds only for constant-ZERO vertices (var exactly 0), i.e. the likely medial-wall case, so the guard works precisely where it is least needed. This is not attenuation but annihilation: one degenerate vertex out of 58 dominates the ROI mean entirely.

Where I narrowed it. The finding's failure narrative targets scripts/detection_floor_table.py. That corruption is not currently realizable. I ran the actual simulation path (build_brain / clip_map, 10 reps of the v3b design, n=15/group, FFCr=58): zero NaNs, minimum se = 1.196e-02, ten orders of magnitude clear of the danger zone. A clean grep across all 8 files in tribe_tools/ (exit 1, completed normally, no truncation) finds no NaN production or handling anywhere in the library. All 32 tests pass. So no already-computed number is wrong; the harm is prospective, not retrospective.

Why it still survives despite that. The bar is "real AND produces a silent wrong result." This is a silent-wrong-result mechanism in the primary replacement for a retracted statistic, in a project whose stated signature bug class is silent failure. MASTER-PLAN.md:392 schedules S2 to compute glm_contrast_z on real TRIBE predictions and report it alongside the sec. 3.1 contrast; that has not run yet, and it is the first time this statistic meets non-synthetic data, eight days from the deadline. Separately and independently of any data pathology, the docstring affirmatively asserts a guarantee the code does not provide, so an auditor checking the degenerate-vertex case is told "handled" when a constant vertex actually yields 1e14. Wrong contract text in the file the paper rests on is itself the defect.

Not critical: nothing published is currently corrupted and the trigger requires data the pipeline has not been shown to produce. Not minor: the failure is undetectable when it occurs, its magnitude is unbounded in the variance case, and the one defense the codebase has (NaN propagation) is defeated for exactly this function.
survivors.correction:
The finding stands, with three adjustments.

1. STRENGTHEN the zero-variance half. It is not limited to "constant only up to float32 rounding (se ~ 1e-17)". A genuinely constant vertex already breaks the documented guarantee, because np.var(ddof=1) of a constant column is nonzero (~1e-32) whenever the value's mean is not exactly representable in binary: np.full(15, 0.7).var(ddof=1) = 1.32e-32. Verified magnitude on a realistic 58-vertex ROI: clean z = 13.977 -> 2.60e14 with one constant vertex. Important carve-out: a constant-ZERO vertex is safe (var is exactly 0.0, guard fires correctly), so the medial-wall / dead-vertex case most likely to occur in fsaverage5 output is the one case that works. The exposure is a constant NONZERO vertex, e.g. a saturated or bias-only readout unit.

2. ADD the silence asymmetry, which is the strongest argument for the "silent" lane. On identical NaN-bearing input, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference and spatial_z all return nan; glm_contrast_z alone returns a finite plausible number. The project's de facto NaN detector is failure-by-propagation in the other statistics, and this function is the single hole in it.

3. NARROW the failure narrative. The claimed corruption of scripts/detection_floor_table.py is not currently realizable and should not be asserted as an active harm: on the real simulation path (build_brain / clip_map, v3b design, 10 reps) there are no NaNs and the minimum se is 1.196e-02. No NaN is produced or handled anywhere in tribe_tools (clean grep over 8 files, exit 1). The correct framing is prospective: the exposure opens when MASTER-PLAN.md:392 runs glm_contrast_z on real TRIBE predictions in S2, plus the standing defect that the docstring states a guarantee the code does not honor.

Also minor: attenuation is not exactly k/58. Zeroing a vertex removes that vertex's own z from the sum, so k/58 holds only in expectation over vertices of equal effect. My run: 15.398 -> 12.336 on 5 vertices, where 4/5 * 15.398 = 12.318.

The proposed fix is sound in shape. Two refinements: the finiteness check should run on the ROI slices av/bv rather than the full arrays, so that NaN in an irrelevant vertex outside the ROI does not raise; and the relative degeneracy test should be scaled by the data magnitude rather than diff alone, e.g. compare se against eps * max(1.0, abs(av).max(), abs(bv).max()), since diff itself is near zero for a vertex that is constant in both conditions and would make the threshold vanish.

survivors.title: glm_contrast_z is documented and named as a z-score but its null SD ranges from 0.14 to 1.06 depending only on inter-vertex correl
survivors.reasoning:
I tried to kill this and could not. Re-derived independently: my own equicorrelated simulation (V=58, na=nb=15, 4000 reps) gives null SD 0.135 / 0.470 / 0.734 / 0.909 / 1.005 / 1.041 at rho = 0 / .2 / .5 / .8 / .95 / 1, matching the finding within MC error, with null mean 0 throughout. The claimed closed form (rho_bar + (1-rho_bar)/V)*df/(df-2) predicts every point to ~1%. Reading roi_stats.py:488-496 confirms the mechanism exactly: per-vertex pooled-SE two-sample t (df = na+nb-2), then z.mean() over ROI columns. So the described behaviour IS what the code does; the statistic is unbiased but its scale is a nuisance parameter.

I then pushed past the finding's own evidence into this repo's actual design. Using scripts/compositional_demo.build_brain at D_AUD=0.24, n=15/group (the v3b design as coded in detection_floor_table.py): mean inter-vertex noise correlation in the FFCr parcel is 0.152 and the measured null SD of glm_contrast_z is 0.473. Comparing the calibrated permutation rule against a naive z>1.96 rule on the identical numbers, power is 0.52 vs 0.03 at a true effect of 0.020, 0.87 vs 0.21 at 0.030, and 1.00 vs 0.90 at 0.050 (the project's own flagship-test effect size). The naive threshold roughly doubles the detection floor, ~0.025 -> ~0.055. A genuine +0.03 FFCr effect would be reported as no selectivity by the normal threshold while the design actually had 87% power — the same shape as the 2026-07-31 retraction, at a venue whose entire topic is this class of error.

Why it clears the "changes a conclusion" bar despite no wrong number today: the docstring at roi_stats.py:461 says "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports", the name says z, the Returns section says "Mean per-vertex z over the ROI" with no scale caveat, ops/interface-contracts.md:443 repeats the framing, and MASTER-PLAN.md:392 commits S2 to "Also compute glm_contrast_z. Report both" for FFC-right, PPA, EBA, VWFA and V1. A number named z, documented as the same quantity a published figure reports, printed beside four other ROIs, will be read on the z scale by the author and by every reviewer. Nothing in the code or tests prevents that. This is a live trap, not a theoretical one.

Two parts of the finding do not hold and I have narrowed them. (1) Its failure narrative asserts "with realistic TRIBE prediction correlation the ROI statistic's null width is well under 1". That is unsupported and arguably backwards: TRIBE predictions are spatially smooth deterministic functions of the stimulus, so across-clip residuals within a 58-vertex parcel plausibly have high rho, which pushes null SD toward 1, not away from it. The rho~0.15 I measured is an artifact of the toy brain's independent per-vertex noise term, not evidence about TRIBE. The honest claim is that the scale is undefined and unmeasured, and wrong in either direction — conservative if rho is low, anti-conservative (6% nominal 5%) if rho is near 1. (2) Its top-end figure 1.057 exceeds the theoretical ceiling sqrt(28/26) = 1.038; immaterial but it should not be pinned in a test as written.

Severity stays minor, at the top of that band. No published or computed number is currently wrong: detection_floor_table.py:75-88 is the sole consumer and it permutes the statistic against itself, which is the correct handling, and tests/test_roi_stats.py:380-395 only pin locality and an arity guard. The fix is a docstring warning plus a rename, costing minutes.
survivors.correction:
Narrower, defensible version:

DEFECT (naming and documentation, not arithmetic). glm_contrast_z returns the arithmetic mean of V per-vertex two-sample t-statistics (df = na+nb-2). Its null distribution is centred at 0 but its null SD is sqrt((rho_bar + (1-rho_bar)/V) * df/(df-2)), where rho_bar is the mean inter-vertex correlation of the across-observation residuals — a nuisance parameter unrelated to the effect. Verified independently at V=58, na=nb=15: SD 0.135 (rho=0), 0.470 (0.2), 0.734 (0.5), 0.909 (0.8), 1.041 (rho=1, the theoretical ceiling sqrt(df/(df-2))=1.038). The value is therefore NOT on the z scale: it cannot be thresholded at 1.96 or 3.1, passed through a normal CDF, or compared numerically to a per-vertex z-map — which is precisely what the docstring's "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" invites.

CONSEQUENCE, quantified in this repo's own design (compositional_demo brain, D_AUD=0.24, n=15/group, FFCr 58 vtx): rho_bar = 0.152, null SD = 0.473. Power of the calibrated permutation test vs a z>1.96 rule: 0.52 vs 0.03 at effect 0.020; 0.87 vs 0.21 at 0.030; 1.00 vs 0.90 at 0.050. The naive threshold roughly doubles the detection floor (~0.025 -> ~0.055), so a real +0.03 effect reads as "no selectivity survives correction".

DROP from the original finding: the assertion that realistic TRIBE correlation makes the null width "well under 1". rho_bar for real TRIBE predictions is unmeasured, and high spatial smoothness argues for rho near 1 (null SD near 1, nominal 5% actually ~6%). The rho~0.15 above is a property of the synthetic brain's independent per-vertex noise, not of TRIBE. State the defect as "scale undefined and unmeasured", wrong in either direction.

FIX (cheap, do before S2):
1. Rename to roi_mean_t (or glm_contrast_meant) in roi_stats.py and ops/interface-contracts.md:443, per CLAUDE.md rule 2.
2. Replace the Returns line with a hard warning: "Mean of per-vertex t-statistics, df = na+nb-2. Its null SD is approximately sqrt(rho_bar + (1-rho_bar)/V) and is NOT 1 — measured 0.14 (rho=0) to 1.04 (rho=1) at V=58, n=15. Must be calibrated by permutation. Never threshold at a normal quantile; never compare numerically to a published per-vertex z-map."
3. Remove or qualify "What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" — it is the sentence that makes the wrong comparison look sanctioned (and it is separately under audit for across-time vs across-observations).
4. Add a test pinning null SD < 0.25 at rho=0 and > 0.85 at rho=0.95 (seeded, V=58, n=15) so the property cannot be forgotten. Do not pin 1.057; the ceiling is 1.038.
5. If S2 must report a thresholdable number, return the ROI-level studentised statistic (t on the ROI-mean timecourse) alongside, and label which is which.

survivors.title: The flagship G020 regression test does not reproduce the case its docstring documents, and fails on 1 in 40 seeds with a misleadin
survivors.reasoning:
Every quantitative claim reproduces exactly under independent re-derivation. At drive seed 7 the test yields realized drive delta 0.1981, raw_d +0.0445, ref_d +0.0463, z_d -0.0562, z_p 0.9875 — versus the docstring's -0.124 / 0.9985. Sweeping the drive seed 0-39 at effect 0.05, seed 8 (realized 0.1437) gives z_d +0.0035, z_p 0.4538, failing both spatial_z assertions; the other 39 pass. Sign crossover at seed 7 sits between effect 0.05 (-0.0562) and 0.08 (+0.0231). Full suite: 32 passed.

However the finding's framing is partly wrong and its consequences are overstated, so it survives only in narrowed form at reduced severity.

(1) I ran scripts/compositional_demo.py, which the finding did not. It prints at effect 0.05 exactly z_d -0.124, z_p 0.9985, raw +0.0446, ref +0.0463. So the docstring's numbers are a truthful quotation of a reproducible source, and the test docstring explicitly attributes them: "Documented case, from the demo's own table". The finding's claim that "the docstring states the pinned case is..." overreads that attribution. No published number is corrupted — the paper's -0.124 / p=0.9985 stands on the demo, which reproduces on demand.

(2) The actual misattribution is in a different file the finding never names: tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:31-37 says the +0.05 case is "Demonstrated in scripts/compositional_demo.py and pinned by tests/test_roi_stats.py::test_spatial_z_inverts_a_real_effect ... spatial_z reports p=0.9985". That "pinned by" is false — the test yields 0.9875 and pins no magnitude.

(3) The CI-flakiness failure mode is speculative. The seed is hard-coded and the test is deterministic today; 39/40 alternative realizations pass, so the construction is ~97.5% robust to realization, not knife-edge. Seed 7's realized delta (0.198) is about -1.1 sd of the realization distribution (sd = 0.10*sqrt(2/15) = 0.037); seed 8 is a -2.6 sd outlier.

(4) The "test would still pass at z_d = -0.001" scenario is real but low-probability here: spatial_z is frozen legacy code carrying a DO-NOT-USE banner, and the second assertion perm_p(z_f, z_n) > 0.5 provides partial (weak) magnitude coverage. Also, if someone "fixed" spatial_z to be non-compositional, z_d would go strongly positive and the sign assertion would fail loudly — the sign-only assertion is not blind to the failure mode it was written for.

What genuinely survives: the flagship G020 regression test pins an artifact 45% the size of the one the codebase advertises, asserts only its sign, and runs ~70% of the way to a sign flip (crossover at effect ~0.075 vs the 0.05 injected) — so a routine retune of the injected effect would produce a false "G020 no longer reproduces" alarm eight days from deadline. Plus one demonstrably false "pinned by" claim in the module docstring that a workshop reviewer could check.
survivors.correction:
Narrowed and corrected version:

The test docstring is NOT wrong — it explicitly credits its numbers to the demo ("Documented case, from the demo's own table"), and I verified scripts/compositional_demo.py prints exactly z_d -0.124, z_p 0.9985, raw +0.0446, ref +0.0463 at effect 0.05. No published number is corrupted.

Two real, narrower defects remain:

(a) FALSE CLAIM IN THE MODULE DOCSTRING, not the test. tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:31-37 states the +0.05 case is "pinned by tests/test_roi_stats.py::test_spatial_z_inverts_a_real_effect ... spatial_z reports p=0.9985". The test does not pin that: it yields z_d = -0.0562, p = 0.9875, and asserts only `z_d < 0` and `p > 0.5`. Fix: change "pinned by" to "demonstrated in scripts/compositional_demo.py; the sign inversion is pinned by tests/...", or strengthen the test to actually pin the magnitude.

(b) THE REGRESSION TEST HAS NO MAGNITUDE BAND AND THIN MARGIN. Because the test hard-codes nominal drive 0.24 but adds rng.normal(0, 0.10) per clip, seed 7 realizes 0.1981, giving an artifact 45% of the documented size, with the sign crossover at effect ~0.075 — only 50% above the 0.05 injected. Confirmed: eff 0.05 -> z_d -0.0562; eff 0.08 -> z_d +0.0231. The practical risk is a FALSE ALARM, not a silent pass: any future retune of the injected effect or the drive would fire "G020 no longer reproduces — investigate" when nothing regressed. Fix (5 minutes): drop the per-clip scatter for this test and use a fixed 0.24 difference (which reproduces the demo's -0.124 regime), then assert a band such as `-0.20 < z_d < -0.05` alongside the existing p > 0.5, and add magnitude bands on the honest statistics (`0.03 < raw_d < 0.06`, `0.03 < ref_d < 0.06`).

Drop from the finding: the NumPy-version-bump flakiness argument (seed is hard-coded, 39/40 realizations pass, and the risk is hypothetical), and the claim that the test could silently accept a scientifically negligible artifact (spatial_z is frozen legacy code with a DO-NOT-USE banner, and `perm_p > 0.5` gives partial coverage).

survivors.title: event_locked_contrast silently drops empty other-category arrays, changing the baseline denominator without notice
survivors.reasoning:
MECHANISM: verified exactly, though the finding's line numbers are wrong (the filter is at roi_stats.py:452, the return at :455, not 300/303). I re-ran the evidence independently: `event_locked_contrast([10.,10.], [[0.,0.],[4.,4.]])` -> 8.0 and `event_locked_contrast([10.,10.], [[],[4.,4.]])` -> 6.0. The filter does silently change the estimand from mean-of-K-category-means to mean-of-(K-1), the guard at :453 fires only when ALL categories are empty, and neither the docstring nor ops/interface-contracts.md:430-433 mentions dropping.

WHAT MAKES IT SURVIVE rather than being cosmetic: I checked what the line is defending against. Without it you get `nan` plus two RuntimeWarnings ("Mean of empty slice", "invalid value encountered in scalar divide"). So the filter is not preventing a crash — it is converting a visible nan into a plausible finite number. That is precisely the failure class this file was written to eliminate; every other new function in it raises loudly (`row_times_from_segments` on a bad object, `_resolve_rows` on an unmatched time, `peri_event_timecourse` on zero onsets, `roi_minus_reference` on ROI/reference overlap, `glm_contrast_z` on n=1). Line 452 is the single place in the new code that silently degrades an estimand, in the function that computes the paper's headline contrast.

WHAT I REFUTED — the failure narrative is mostly wrong. Two of the three named upstream causes cannot produce an empty array, because the library's own producer refuses to:
  - "a manifest typo" / category with zero onsets -> `event_locked_response` -> `peri_event_timecourse` raises ValueError("no event onsets given"). Confirmed by running.
  - "a category with all onsets outside the window" -> `_resolve_rows` raises IndexError("N of M requested times have no prediction row within 0.5 s"). Confirmed by running.
So the only live path is a caller that builds per-category arrays by label-masking a response vector (`resp[labels == c]`) instead of calling `event_locked_response` per category. No such caller exists: grep over scripts/, tribe_tools/, tests/, ops/, .notes/ finds the symbol only in its own definition, the docstring cross-reference at :43, two tests, and the plan/contract docs. S2 is unwritten. The branch is currently dead.

MAGNITUDE — the finding's 25% is a toy-example artifact, but the realistic number is not negligible either. At the 5-category S2 design (faces vs bodies/places/objects/characters, K=4 others) dropping the lowest category shifts the contrast by (m_dropped - mean_rest)/K; with plausible category means I get ~3%, which would not flip a permutation test. But MASTER-PLAN.md:388-390 says the 5-category design costs 7.2 h of video and explicitly offers the fallback "cut to 3 categories (faces, objects, places)". In that configuration K=2, and losing one category replaces the baseline with a single category's mean — a distortion of tens of percent, i.e. genuinely conclusion-capable. The severity therefore rests on a design choice that is still open, not on a settled one.

VERDICT: real, correctly described at the code level, currently unreachable through the library's own API, but a one-line latent trap in the function the S2 caller will be written against in the next ten days, in a file whose entire design contract is "never return a plausible wrong number". Minor is the right severity — it is a hardening fix, not a live corruption. It should not be sold as an active bias toward NO-GO.
survivors.correction:
Narrowed version: `event_locked_contrast` (tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:452) filters out empty other-category arrays and then averages the survivors, silently changing the estimand from mean-of-K-category-means to mean-of-(K-1). Verified: ([10,10], [[0,0],[4,4]]) = 8.0 vs ([10,10], [[],[4,4]]) = 6.0. Without the filter the result would be a visible nan, so the line actively converts a detectable failure into an undetectable one — the one place in this new file that does not fail loudly.

Drop the finding's stated failure scenarios: an empty category cannot arise from the library's own producer. Zero onsets raise ValueError("no event onsets given") in `peri_event_timecourse`; onsets outside the window raise IndexError in `_resolve_rows`. Both confirmed by execution. The only reachable path is a future caller that slices responses by a category label vector, and no caller exists yet (grep over scripts/, tribe_tools/, tests/, ops/, .notes/ finds no production use).

Drop the "biases toward NO-GO" claim as unsupported: it presumes characters/VWFA is the lowest-responding FFC category, which is not established here, and at the 5-category design the resulting shift is ~3% of the contrast. The case for fixing it is the 3-category fallback in MASTER-PLAN.md:388-390 (faces/objects/places), where K=2 and dropping one category replaces the baseline with a single category mean — a tens-of-percent distortion.

Fix as proposed (raise on any empty other-category array, naming the count), plus one line in the docstring and in ops/interface-contracts.md:430 stating that every other-category array must be non-empty because the baseline is a mean over CATEGORIES. Also correct the finding's line citations: 452 and 455, not 300 and 303.

survivors.title: detection_floor reports a solvable configuration error as a scientific conclusion when alpha < 1/(n_perm+1)
survivors.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not refute the mechanism, only its stated blast radius.

RE-DERIVED, ALL CONFIRMED:
1. `mc_perm_p` returns `(ge + 1) / (n_perm + 1)` (roi_stats.py:160), floor 1/(n_perm+1). `detection_floor.achieved_power` (roi_stats.py:585-593) tests `mc_perm_p(...) <= alpha`. If alpha < 1/(n_perm+1) the comparison is unsatisfiable, achieved_power is identically 0, and the bracketing loop (roi_stats.py:596-606) doubles hi from noise_sd to >1e6 (~21 doublings) and raises.
2. Validation at roi_stats.py:536-541 checks only `0 < alpha < 1`. There is no alpha-vs-n_perm check anywhere. Confirmed by reading.
3. Ran it: `detection_floor(30, noise_sd=1.0, alpha=0.004, n_sim=5, n_perm=200)` raises in 0.36 s with exactly the quoted text, including "the design is underpowered for any plausible effect; report that, do not run it". The design is not underpowered — analytic two-sample MDE at n=30/group, alpha=0.004, 80% power is ~0.90 sd (the finding says 0.79; either way it is ~1 sd, not >1e6). Raising alpha to 0.006 (just above 1/201 = 0.004975) makes the same call return a finite floor of 1.06. So the trigger is precisely the n_perm boundary, not the design.
4. Boundary arithmetic checks out: 1/401 = 0.0024938. `detection_floor(15, sd=1, alpha=0.025/6=0.004167, n_perm=400)` returns 1.369 (no raise); `alpha=0.001, n_perm=400` raises. So the crossover is where the finding says it is.
5. The message omits `n_perm` — the one parameter at fault — from the parameters it prints, which is what makes it actively misdirecting rather than merely terse.

WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES (why it stays minor, not higher):
- It is loud, never silent. It raises; it does not return a wrong floor. Nothing can be quietly published from it.
- No publication path touches it. `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` — the script that actually writes `data/floor_table_v3b.md` — does not import or call `detection_floor`; it rolls its own grid + `interpolate_floor` at ALPHA=0.025, N_PERM=500. Grep across scripts/, tribe_tools/, neurocheck/, brainlens/ finds only the definition, one docstring cross-reference (line 45), and tests/test_roi_stats.py:412-418 (which use alpha default 0.025 with n_perm=200, boundary 0.004975 — safely clear). Callers: zero.
- The stated failure scenario (5-6 ROIs x 2 IUT contrasts Bonferroni'd to 0.0025) contradicts the project's own doctrine. `iut_pass` (roi_stats.py:171-178) states the IUT "controls the family-wise error at alpha without further correction", and the pre-registered level is alpha=0.025 (detection_floor_table.py:41). Bonferroni over >=11 tests is not this project's declared regime, so that specific route is speculative.

WHAT KEEPS IT ALIVE ANYWAY: a realistic non-exotic trigger exists that the finding did not name. `n_perm` is a pure compute knob on a machine with borrowed CPU-only compute, and lowering it to speed up a floor scan silently invalidates strict alphas: `alpha=0.005` (the "redefine significance" level) with `n_perm=100` (boundary 0.0099) raises the same false verdict, as does `alpha=0.001` at the default n_perm=400. An operator exploring a stricter threshold, in a project whose doctrine is "no verdict without a floor", is told in the imperative that the design is hopeless and to report that. That is a diagnostic making a false scientific assertion, which is worth two lines of guard ten days out.

ALSO: the proposed fix is right but incomplete, and its advice is wrong in one case. The achievable-p bound is max(1/(n_perm+1), ~1/C(2n,n)) — the rank permutation null has its own floor from the design. Verified: at n=3/group, C(6,3)=20, perfect separation yields p ~= 0.040-0.048 at every n_perm I tried (20, 100, 400, 5000), so `detection_floor(3, sd=1, alpha=0.025, n_perm=400)` raises and there the message is TRUE — no n_perm helps. The proposed guard would not fire there (1/401 < 0.025), leaving that case as-is (harmless, message is correct); but at n=3 with n_perm=20 the guard WOULD fire and advise "increase n_perm to at least 40", which is actively wrong advice for a design that can never reach 0.025.
survivors.correction:
Narrower, corrected statement:

`detection_floor` never validates `alpha` against the smallest p-value its own test can return. When `alpha < 1/(n_perm+1)`, `achieved_power` is identically zero, the bracketing loop doubles to `max_effect`, and the RuntimeError at roi_stats.py:601-606 asserts "the design is underpowered for any plausible effect; report that, do not run it" while omitting `n_perm` — the parameter actually at fault — from the parameters it prints. The design is typically fine (n=30/group at alpha=0.004 has an analytic MDE of ~0.9 sd).

Impact is a MISLEADING DIAGNOSTIC, not a corrupted number: it raises loudly, and no publication script calls it today (`scripts/detection_floor_table.py` implements its own power grid and never imports `detection_floor`; the only callers in the repo are two tests). The finding's Bonferroni-over-10-ROIs scenario also runs against the project's own IUT doctrine (roi_stats.py:171-178, "without further correction") and the pre-registered alpha=0.025. The realistic trigger is instead an operator lowering `n_perm` to save CPU while scanning a strict alpha — e.g. alpha=0.005 with n_perm=100, or alpha=0.001 with the default n_perm=400 — both of which I confirmed raise the false message.

The fix should guard both floors, not just n_perm, and must not give impossible advice:

    min_mc = 1.0 / (n_perm + 1)
    min_exact = 1.0 / comb(2 * n_per_group, n_per_group)
    if alpha < min_exact:
        raise ValueError(
            f"alpha={alpha} is below the smallest p-value a label permutation test can "
            f"reach at n={n_per_group} per group (1/C({2*n_per_group},{n_per_group})="
            f"{min_exact:.2e}); no n_perm fixes this — the DESIGN cannot detect anything "
            f"at this alpha."
        )
    if alpha <= min_mc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"alpha={alpha} is at or below mc_perm_p's smallest return value "
            f"1/(n_perm+1)={min_mc:.6f}; this is a resolution limit of n_perm, not a "
            f"property of the design — raise n_perm to at least {int(np.ceil(1/alpha))}."
        )

The two branches matter: at n=3/group, perfect separation yields p ~= 0.04-0.05 at every n_perm from 20 to 5000, so the finding's single-branch fix would tell that user to raise n_perm when nothing would help.

survivors.title: define_froi's independence rule is warn-only, and using the test data as its own localizer gives a 100% false-positive rate
survivors.reasoning:
FACTUAL CLAIM: fully reproduces. I re-derived it from scratch rather than trusting the evidence.

1. Code reading (roi_stats.py:499-541). `define_froi(loc_a, loc_b, parcel_verts, top_n)` accepts any two arrays, averages 2-D inputs over axis 0, computes `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]`, and returns `np.sort(pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]])` — a bare int array. The only independence enforcement is the `.. warning::` block at lines 509-514. No runtime check, no provenance in the return value. Confirmed.

2. Independent re-run (20 null datasets, n=15/condition, 1000 vertices, 300-vertex parcel, both conditions N(0.6,0.05), perm_p with n_perm=499):
   - double-dip (fROI defined on the same arrays then tested on them): p = 0.002 on all 20, i.e. 1/(n_perm+1), the MC floor. 20/20 false positives at alpha=0.025.
   - honest split-half (fROI from rows 0-6, tested on rows 7-14): 0/20 false positives, p ranging 0.08-0.98.
   The arithmetic explains the determinism: selecting the top 100 of 300 vertices by mean difference yields a ROI-mean difference of ~1.09 x sd_pervertex_diff ≈ 0.020, while the permutation null sd of the 100-vertex ROI mean difference is 0.05/sqrt(100)*sqrt(2/15) ≈ 0.0018. That is ~11 sigma by construction. The floor p-value is not stochastic; it is guaranteed.

3. Repo state. grep over tribe_tools/, scripts/, tests/, ops/ (scoped, with --include filters, completed cleanly): `define_froi` has NO production caller. It appears only at its definition, in ops/interface-contracts.md:447, and in two tests. Confirmed that neither test touches independence — test_define_froi_picks_the_selective_vertices checks ranking, test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size checks the cap. Confirmed no split-half helper exists anywhere in the repo.

4. Internal precedent, which the finding missed and which strengthens it: the sibling function `roi_minus_reference` (line 207) makes the analogous methodological guard STRUCTURAL — it raises ValueError on `np.intersect1d(verts, ref_verts).size` with the message "ROI and reference overlap ... or this is an undeclared normaliser". The same module, written in the same pass, hard-fails on the less dangerous of the two circularity errors and only warns on the more dangerous one. That inconsistency is a real, substantiable gap in the module's own standard.

5. Pressure is real, not hypothetical. MASTER-PLAN S2 (line 393) does say "Define the face fROI from half the exemplars, test on the other half," and lines 388-390 show exemplar counts already being cut for GPU cost (5x50 -> 3x50 or 5x25). Halving 25 exemplars leaves 12-13 for the localizer. Hand-managed split bookkeeping under that pressure is exactly where slips happen.

WHERE THE FINDING IS OVERSTATED (why I am lowering severity from major):

- "Silently available", "no warning": inaccurate as stated. The requirement is documented twice and explicitly — in the docstring warning and in ops/interface-contracts.md, which literally records "Warn-only; the caller is responsible for the split." This was a recorded design decision, not an oversight. It is silent at RUNTIME only.
- It is not a defect in `define_froi`. The function computes exactly what its contract says. Independence is a property of how the caller partitioned exemplars, and no signature can verify it in general. The finding's proposed fix (1), a `localizer_is_independent: bool` with no default, is an honor-system speed bump that a rushed caller passes True to; fix (3), hashing, catches only the literally-identical-array case and not the realistic partial-overlap or test-on-full-set slips. Only fix (2), a helper that owns the partition, is genuinely structural.
- Every top-N vertex/voxel selection routine in every neuroimaging toolbox has this property. The 20/20 demonstration is a demonstration of Kriegeskorte-style circular analysis, not of a bug unique to this code.
- No number is currently corrupted and no scientific conclusion is currently affected: the function is unreached outside tests and S2 has not been run.

Net: real, reproducible, worth fixing before S2 runs, but it is a missing guardrail on an unreached function whose requirement is already documented twice — not a wrong result present in the code. Minor.
survivors.correction:
Narrower, substantiated version:

`define_froi` (tribe_tools/roi_stats.py:499) enforces its independence requirement by docstring only, while the sibling function `roi_minus_reference` (line 207) hard-raises on the analogous circularity error (ROI/reference overlap). That inconsistency is the defect worth fixing — not "the code produces a false positive," which it does not do on its own. Two concrete, cheap items:

1.
