findings.title: The floor table's nuisance level D_AUD=0.24 is the top edge of the search grid, not the fitted optimum it is described as
findings.claim: D_AUD = 0.24 is documented in three places as "the auditory drive difference that best matches the observed 2026-07-31 pattern (0.24, sum-sq error 0.081)". 0.24 is the last point of compositional_demo.py's search grid `np.arange(0.0, 0.25, 0.01)`. Widening the grid shows the error surface is flat past that edge and reaches a lower value beyond it, so 0.24 is where the search stopped, not where the fit optimises.
findings.evidence: scripts/compositional_demo.py:186 — `for d_aud in np.arange(0.0, 0.25, 0.01):` (last value 0.24). detection_floor_table.py:10 and :39 — "at the auditory drive difference that best matches the observed 2026-07-31 pattern (0.24, sum-sq error 0.081)" / `D_AUD = 0.24        # best match to the observed 2026-07-31 pattern`. tests/test_roi_stats.py:170-172 repeats it. I re-ran the identical fit with perm_p stubbed (mc_perm_p builds its own seeded RNG and does not consume compositional_demo's module-level RNG, so the state sequence is preserved) after replicating main()'s six warm-up run() calls, over d_aud = 0.00..0.44: err = 0.0810 at d=0.24 with FFCr −0.239 (reproduces the documented numbers exactly), but err = 0.0765 at d=0.33 (FFCr −0.284), and the surface is flat across the whole range 0.24–0.40 (0.0765 to 0.0846). MASTER-PLAN §3.3 / D026 quote the sim value −0.239 against observed −0.244.
findings.concrete_failure: spatial_z's detection floor is the only column of the floor table that depends on D_AUD (raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference and glm_contrast_z are insensitive to auditory drive by construction), and it is precisely the column the write-up leans on — the script's own output text calls it "the number that makes the 2026-07-31 verdict uninterpretable". Setting that nuisance level by where a loop happened to stop, while calling it a fit, is M001's error in a new costume: the acceptance number is read off the search proxy instead of measured on the delivered quantity. Any reviewer who re-runs the sweep one step wider gets a different headline floor for the retracted statistic.
findings.fix: Widen compositional_demo's sweep until the error surface actually turns, and report the profile rather than a point — the surface is flat from 0.24 to 0.40, which is itself the honest finding and should be stated. Then either justify D_AUD as a disclosed chosen level (not a fit) or report the floor table at three levels (e.g. 0.10 / 0.24 / 0.35) as a sensitivity check, and correct the wording in all three places that say "best matches".

findings.title: Two divergent MDE estimators: the shipped floor table never calls the tested detection_floor, and detection_floor's docstring overstates what it simulates
findings.claim: detection_floor() is the function S1 asked for and the only MDE code with a test, but the script that produces the floors does not import or call it. The script implements a second, untested estimator (fixed effect grid plus linear interpolation of the first power crossing). Separately, detection_floor's docstring claims it runs "the same one-sided permutation test the verdict uses", which is not true for at least glm_contrast_z.
findings.evidence: detection_floor_table.py:31-37 imports `glm_contrast_z, perm_p, raw_roi_mean, roi_minus_reference, spatial_z` — detection_floor is absent. Floors come from `interpolate_floor` (:87-96), which returns the FIRST crossing `powers[i] >= target > powers[i-1]` and is covered by no test (scoped grep of tests/ for 'detection_floor_table' returns nothing). roi_stats.py:435-443 always uses `mc_perm_p` (Mann-Whitney U on per-group scalars) inside `achieved_power`, against roi_stats.py:438-439 "This simulates the design's own test — the same one-sided permutation test the verdict uses". But detection_floor_table.py:71-83 explicitly builds a DIFFERENT null for glm_contrast_z — "glm_contrast_z is a single across-clip number, not a per-clip value, so its permutation null shuffles the clip labels and recomputes it each time" — which detection_floor cannot express.
findings.concrete_failure: The floors that go into the paper come from the untested path; the tested path (test_detection_floor_scales_the_right_way) guards code nothing else calls. If the two estimators disagree, nothing catches it. And because interpolate_floor takes the first crossing of a Monte-Carlo power estimate at N_SIM=100, a single noisy grid point below target can push the reported floor to a higher effect with no warning.
findings.fix: Either have the script call detection_floor for the three per-clip statistics (leaving glm_contrast_z's bespoke null documented as the exception), or add a test asserting the two estimators agree within tolerance on a case both can express. Correct detection_floor's docstring to say it simulates the Mann-Whitney permutation test on per-observation values, and state which statistics that covers.

lanes.lane_summary: I ran the suite (26 passing at session start; the file was rewritten under me mid-audit and it is now 32 passing), then attacked it three ways: (1) a 40-seed sensitivity sweep of the two spatial_z regression tests, (2) a line-by-line numeric diff of the test's `_synthetic_brain`/`_clip` against `scripts/compositional_demo.py`'s `build_brain`/`clip_map`, and (3) mutation testing — 15 plausible, scientifically-meaningful defects injected into the code under test, run against the full suite in an isolated sandbox. Result: 10 of 15 mutations SURVIVE. The suite is strong exactly where it was written to be strong (the lag/row-drift/timing code added today is well covered — 5 of 5 mutations there and in `event_locked_contrast`/`roi_minus_reference` were killed) and near-vacuous everywhere else. Two headline results: replacing the entire body of `glm_contrast_z` with `return 0.0` passes all 32 tests, and `detection_floor` — the number D-3 requires beside every verdict — survives having its alpha silently hardcoded, its bisection return inverted, and its effect size halved. On the duplicated synthetic brain: I confirmed the two implementations are numerically IDENTICAL today (same base array, same spatial_z to 1e-12 for matched drive/seed), so the test currently pins the same artifact the demo demonstrates; the risk is latent drift, not a present error. Seed sensitivity of the flagship test is 39/40, not "seed 7 only" — but the case it actually runs is not the case its docstring documents, and 1/40 seeds flips the sign and fires the misleading message "G020 no longer reproduces — investigate". I found no circular pinning: the documented numbers come from the demo's independently-inlined statistics, and the hand-computed assertions (`event_locked_contrast` = 8.0, `define_froi` = 150..159) are genuinely derived by hand. `glm_contrast_z` itself is CORRECT (matches scipy's pooled two-sample t to 1e-9) — every finding below is about false confidence, not a live wrong number, except where noted.
lanes.search_failures: No search or tool call was killed, truncated, or errored; all greps were path-scoped and all scripts ran to completion. Two environment facts that materially affect this audit and must not be hidden: (1) `tribe_tools/roi_stats.py` was REWRITTEN on disk at 08:48 UTC while I was auditing it — it grew from 462 lines to 613, `event_locked_response` changed signature from `(preds, verts, onsets_tr, lag_trs=5)` to `(preds, verts, onset_times_s, row_times_s, lag_trs=0)`, and `row_times_from_segments`/`_resolve_rows`/`peri_event_timecourse`/`peak_lag_trs` were added; `tests/test_roi_stats.py` went 304 -> 419 lines at the same time. I detected this because an isolated import produced a signature that did not match the file I had read, re-read everything, and re-ran every check against the current on-disk version — all findings below are against the CURRENT file (md5 1cfe32d83f3bf40a00080d18eb17745b, 26218 bytes). A concurrent writer is active on this repo; if it commits again, re-verify. (2) The task brief states the suite "currently passes 40" with "11 new tests"; the actual counts are 26 passing / 13 new at session start and 32 passing / 19 new now. Whatever produced "40" was not this file.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z has zero value coverage — replacing its entire body with `return 0.0` passes all 32 tests
findings.claim: Neither glm_contrast_z test constrains the value the function returns. The 'unmoved by a distant region' test is tautological: glm_contrast_z's first computational line is `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]`, so columns outside `verts` are sliced away before any arithmetic and CANNOT influence the result. The test mutates `a2[:, 200:]` while `roi = np.arange(0, 50)` — it asserts that NumPy fancy-indexing works, not that the statistic is non-compositional. The second test only checks an input-validation raise. Together they leave the entire estimator unpinned.
findings.evidence: I replaced everything from `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]` to the end of the function with `return 0.0` and ran the suite in an isolated sandbox: `glm_contrast_z body replaced by 'return 0.0' -> 32 passed in 3.92s`. Targeted mutations confirm the same: `se = np.sqrt(var * (1.0/na + 1.0/nb))` -> `se = np.sqrt(var)` SURVIVED (32 passed); `av.var(axis=0, ddof=1)` -> `ddof=0` SURVIVED; adding `z[~ok] = diff[~ok]` (zero-variance vertices leaking their raw difference instead of contributing 0, contradicting the docstring's 'Vertices with zero pooled variance contribute 0 rather than inf') SURVIVED. Measured impact of the first: on (12,30) data, glm_contrast_z = 12.604861, mutant = 5.145913 — a 2.449x scale error (1/sqrt(1/12+1/12)). For the record, the shipped implementation is CORRECT: it equals the mean per-vertex scipy `ttest_ind(..., equal_var=True).statistic` to 1e-9 (12.604861 vs 12.604861).
findings.concrete_failure: glm_contrast_z is one of the four statistics in `scripts/detection_floor_table.py`, whose docstring promises 'Units are RAW predicted-response units throughout, so the four statistics are directly comparable'. A 2.449x scale error in its z — the exact off-by-sqrt(1/na+1/nb) confusion between a z-statistic and Cohen's d — would silently rescale the `glm_contrast_z` column of `data/floor_table_v3b.md` and make the paper's cross-statistic floor comparison wrong by a factor of 2.4, with the whole suite green. Worse, it is the statistic the paper cites as 'what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports'; a mis-scaled z published against Meta's figure is a second retractable error.
findings.fix: Add a value test with an independent oracle, not a self-comparison: `assert abs(glm_contrast_z(a, b, roi) - np.mean([scipy.stats.ttest_ind(a[:, v], b[:, v], equal_var=True).statistic for v in roi])) < 1e-9` (scipy is already a dependency — the test file's `_hrf` imports from math, and scipy is importable in this env). Add a hand-computed two-vertex case with known na, nb. Add a test that a zero-variance vertex contributes exactly 0. Replace the tautological distant-region test with the one that carries the scientific claim: build data where a distant region shifts, and assert that spatial_z MOVES while glm_contrast_z does not — that is the G020 contrast, and it is currently untested for glm_contrast_z.

findings.title: detection_floor's returned number is completely unpinned — alpha can be ignored, the bisection inverted, and the MDE doubled, all silently
findings.claim: The only test of detection_floor asserts two orderings (`small_n > large_n > 0` and `louder > small_n`). Every defect that rescales or shifts the floor uniformly passes, because uniform rescaling preserves ordering. The function's own docstring says 'the floor goes in the paper' and D-3 says 'No verdict without a floor' — yet no test states what the floor should be for any input.
findings.evidence: Mutations run against the full suite: (a) `return float(hi)` -> `return float(lo)` at the end of the bisection SURVIVED (32 passed); (b) `... <= alpha` -> `... <= 0.05` inside `achieved_power`, i.e. the `alpha` argument silently ignored, SURVIVED; (c) `a = rng.normal(effect, noise_sd, n_per_group)` -> `rng.normal(effect * 0.5, ...)`, a clean 2x error in the reported MDE, SURVIVED. I also measured the true values: at the test's own settings (n_sim=60, n_perm=200, tol=0.02) across seeds 0-7 the floor is n=6: [1.906, 2.047, 1.891, 1.812, 1.984, 2.234, 1.953, 1.969] (spread 0.422, 21% of the value); n=15: mean 1.133, spread 0.156; n=24: mean 0.869, spread 0.188. At library defaults (n_sim=200, n_perm=400) n=15 gives [1.083, 1.1045, 1.1055, 1.1045] — stable to 0.02. The analytic two-sample MDE (z_0.975 + z_0.80)*sd*sqrt(2/n) is 1.617 / 1.023 / 0.809 for n = 6 / 15 / 24, so the implementation is ~7-8% conservative at n=15, which is the right order for a rank-based permutation test (ARE 0.955).
findings.concrete_failure: detection_floor(15, noise_sd=1.0) returns 1.10 today. Under mutation (c) it returns ~2.2 and the suite stays green. The paper then reports 'this design could not have detected any FFCr effect smaller than 2.2 raw units' when the true floor is 1.1 — a claim that is twice as pessimistic as reality, published as the corrective for the retracted 2026-07-31 NO-GO. Under mutation (b) the floor is computed at alpha=0.05 while the pre-registered verdict runs at alpha=0.025, so the stated floor is systematically too small and the paper claims more sensitivity than the design has. Both are the same class of error as the retraction: an unvalidated primary number.
findings.fix: Pin the value against the analytic oracle, which is available in closed form: `assert 0.85 * an < detection_floor(n, sd, ...) < 1.30 * an` where `an = (norm.ppf(1-alpha) + norm.ppf(power)) * sd * sqrt(2/n)` — measured values sit at 1.08-1.22x of `an`, so that band is both true and tight enough to kill all three mutations. Add `assert detection_floor(n, sd, alpha=0.05, ...) < detection_floor(n, sd, alpha=0.005, ...)` to make `alpha` load-bearing, and `assert detection_floor(n, sd, power=0.5, ...) < detection_floor(n, sd, power=0.9, ...)` for `power`. Also raise the test's `n_sim` above 60 or widen `tol`: at n_sim=60 the returned floor has a 0.42 seed-to-seed spread at n=6, so no tight value assertion is possible at the settings the test currently uses.

findings.title: The flagship G020 regression test does not reproduce the case its docstring documents, and fails on 1 in 40 seeds with a misleading message
findings.claim: The docstring states the pinned case is 'true effect 0.05 -> spatial_z delta -0.124, p=0.9985'. The test actually produces z_d = -0.0562, p = 0.9875 — the artifact it reproduces is 45% of the documented magnitude. The cause is that the test hard-codes the NOMINAL auditory-drive difference 0.24 but adds `rng.normal(0, 0.10)` scatter to each of 15+15 clips, and at seed 7 the REALIZED difference is 0.1981, not 0.24. Because z_d is close to linear in the realized drive difference, the artifact shrinks proportionally. The test asserts only `z_d < 0`, so it silently accepts an artifact of any size, including one two-thirds smaller than documented — and at some seeds, no artifact at all.
findings.evidence: Against the current module: `drive seed 7: raw +0.0445 ref +0.0463 z_d -0.0562 z_p 0.9875 -> test PASSES`; the docstring claims `z_d -0.124, z_p 0.9985`. Note raw (+0.0445 vs +0.0446) and ref (+0.0463 vs +0.0463) match the docstring almost exactly — only z_d is off, confirming the drive realization is the cause. Realized drive delta at seed 7 = 0.1981 vs nominal 0.24. Sweeping only the drive seed over 0-39 at effect 0.05: 39/40 pass, but seed 8 gives realized delta 0.1437, z_d = +0.0035, z_p = 0.4538 -> BOTH final assertions fail. Sign-flip proximity at seed 7: effect 0.00 -> z_d -0.1884, 0.05 -> -0.0562, 0.08 -> +0.0231. The injected 0.05 sits ~70% of the way to the crossover, so the test runs with far less margin than the -0.124 in its docstring implies.
findings.concrete_failure: On a CI machine, a NumPy version bump that perturbs `default_rng(7).normal` stream consumption, or any future edit that adds one RNG draw before the loop, shifts the realized drive and can land on a seed-8-like realization. The test then fails with `AssertionError: G020 no longer reproduces — investigate` — telling a solo researcher eight days from an ICBINB-BIO deadline that the paper's central finding has stopped reproducing, when nothing regressed at all. Conversely, and worse for the paper, the test as written would still pass if a future change reduced the artifact to z_d = -0.001, i.e. if G020 had become scientifically negligible.
findings.fix: Make the artifact deterministic and pin its magnitude. Either drop the per-clip drive scatter for this test (use a fixed 0.24 difference, which is the setting the docstring cites) or keep the scatter and assert on the realized quantity. Then replace `assert z_d < 0` with a band that matches what is actually produced, e.g. `assert -0.20 < z_d < -0.03`, and correct the docstring to the numbers the test really yields (-0.056 / p=0.9875) or re-tune the construction until it yields -0.124. Also assert the magnitudes of the honest statistics (`0.03 < raw_d < 0.06`, `0.03 < ref_d < 0.06`) instead of only their sign — currently `raw_d > 0` is nearly free, since a +0.05 additive injection into the ROI mean cannot plausibly come out negative.

findings.title: define_froi's tests cannot distinguish a selectivity contrast from raw amplitude — ignoring loc_b entirely passes both
findings.claim: Both fROI tests set `loc_b` to an all-zero array, so `a[pv] - b[pv]` and `a[pv]` are numerically identical and the tests cannot tell a contrast-based fROI from a raw-amplitude-based one. That is precisely the distinction the function exists to make: its docstring promises 'Top-N most A-selective vertices inside a parcel', and ranking by raw A response instead selects the highest-amplitude vertices, which in this brain model are the auditory-mass vertices, not the selective ones.
findings.evidence: Mutation `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]` -> `sel = a[pv]` SURVIVED (32 passed). In `test_define_froi_picks_the_selective_vertices`, `b = np.zeros(500)` and in `test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size` both arguments are `np.zeros(10)`. By contrast the direction mutation `np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]` -> `np.argsort(sel)[:k]` WAS killed, so only the ranking direction is covered, not the quantity being ranked. Neither test exercises the 2D `(n_obs, n_vertices)` path (`a = a.mean(axis=0) if a.ndim == 2 else a`), and no test covers a parcel whose vertices are non-contiguous or unsorted.
findings.concrete_failure: Feed the real localizer a `loc_b` with structure — e.g. FFCr responds 0.62 to faces and 0.60 to objects while the auditory mass responds 1.00 to both. The correct contrast picks the 58 FFCr vertices (sel = +0.02) over auditory (sel = 0.00). A raw-amplitude ranking picks 100 auditory vertices (sel = 1.00) and returns them as the 'face fROI'. Every downstream contrast is then computed on auditory cortex, and the paper reports face selectivity — or its absence — from the wrong region, with the suite green. This is the ROI-definition twin of the statistic error the project already retracted once.
findings.fix: Give `loc_b` real structure in the test: set `a[140:150] = 3.0; b[140:150] = 3.0` (high amplitude, zero selectivity) alongside `a[150:160] = 1.0; b[150:160] = 0.0` (low amplitude, genuinely selective) and assert `define_froi(a, b, parcel, top_n=10).tolist() == list(range(150, 160))`. That single change kills the `sel = a[pv]` mutation. Add a 2D-input test asserting the `(n_obs, n_vertices)` path averages over observations, and a test that the returned indices are always a subset of `parcel_verts` for an unsorted, non-contiguous parcel.

findings.title: _resolve_rows' 0.5 s tolerance is untested at its boundary — widening it to 5 s (five TRs of silent misalignment) passes the suite
findings.claim: The `tol` parameter in `_resolve_rows` is the single guard preventing silently-misaligned event reads, and no test constrains it. The only loudness test requests t=100.0 s against rows spanning 0-9 s — a 90-second error, roughly 180x the tolerance. Any tolerance from 0.5 s up to ~90 s passes that test identically, so the guard's actual threshold is unpinned.
findings.evidence: Mutation `def _resolve_rows(row_times_s, want_s, tol: float = 0.5)` -> `tol: float = 5.0` SURVIVED (32 passed). The test's fixture is `times = np.arange(0.0, 10.0)` with `onset_times_s=[100.0]`: the nearest row is at 9.0 s, an error of 91.0 s. `test_event_locked_response_resolves_by_time_not_row_index` uses exact hits (error 0.0). No test sits anywhere near the 0.5 s boundary in either direction.
findings.concrete_failure: TR is 1.0 s (ops/source-of-truth.md, verified). A 5 s tolerance means an onset at t=20.0 s silently resolves to the prediction row at t=25.0 s — five TRs late, reading past the HRF peak at ~18% amplitude, which is the exact failure `event_locked_response`'s own warning quantifies as '5.5x attenuation that would fail the detection floor and fire the S2 stop rule on a real effect'. The function was written specifically to prevent this class of silent misalignment (M001), the suite has a well-built regression test for the row-drift version of it, and yet the numeric guard itself is free to drift to any value under 90 s.
findings.fix: Add two boundary tests against `times = np.arange(0.0, 10.0)`: `event_locked_response(preds, verts, onset_times_s=[3.4], row_times_s=times, lag_trs=0)` must resolve to the row at 3.0 s, and `onset_times_s=[3.6]` with the rows thinned so the nearest is 0.6 s away must raise `IndexError` matching 'no prediction row within'. Assert the error message reports the actual offset, since the message quotes `off by {err:.3f} s` and downstream debugging depends on it.

findings.title: The zero-face-information test's second assertion compares two different units and has 72x of headroom
findings.claim: `assert abs(raw_d) < abs(z_d), 'the raw statistic should stay near zero'` compares a raw predicted-response difference against a spatial-z difference. These are different units — spatial_z divides by the brain-wide sd, which is ~0.36 in this synthetic brain — so the assertion is satisfied by the unit mismatch alone, not by raw_roi_mean staying near zero. It cannot detect a raw-statistic artifact until that artifact is 72x its current size.
findings.evidence: Computed on the test's exact construction (brain seed 0, drive seed 11, clip seeds 3000+i / 4000+i): raw_d = +0.00409, z_d = -0.29465, mean brain sd = 0.3641. The assertion compares 0.00409 against 0.29465, leaving a factor of 72 of headroom. Converting to comparable units, the artifact is z_d * sd = 0.10729 raw units versus raw_d = 0.00409 — a true ratio of 26x, not 72x. The stated intent ('the raw statistic should stay near zero') is a claim about raw_d in absolute terms, which the assertion never makes.
findings.concrete_failure: If a future change to raw_roi_mean introduced a condition-dependent artifact of, say, 0.05 raw units — the same size as the genuine face effect the flagship test injects, and enough to fabricate a significant result on its own — `abs(0.05) < abs(0.295)` still holds and the test passes while asserting in its own message that the raw statistic stayed near zero. The suite would then endorse an artifact-carrying replacement for the statistic that was retracted for carrying an artifact.
findings.fix: Assert the intended claim directly and in raw units: `assert abs(raw_d) < 0.01, 'raw must stay near zero'` (measured 0.00409, so 0.01 is a true and tight bound), and separately `assert z_d < -0.15` to pin the artifact's magnitude rather than only its sign. If a relative comparison is wanted, convert first: `assert abs(raw_d) < 0.2 * abs(z_d) * brain_sd`.

findings.title: raw_roi_mean has no direct value test — swapping its mean for a median passes the suite
findings.claim: raw_roi_mean is only ever used inside other tests as a comparator, never asserted against a known value. Its aggregation over the ROI is therefore unconstrained.
findings.evidence: Mutation `return float(g[verts].mean())` -> `return float(np.median(g[verts]))` SURVIVED (32 passed). The three tests that call raw_roi_mean assert only `> 0`, `abs(...) > 3.9` (an additive shift, which a median preserves exactly), and the unit-mismatched comparison in the finding above — none pins the aggregation. There is also no test of the 1D-input branch or of the `empty ROI vertex set` raise.
findings.concrete_failure: raw_roi_mean is the 'simplest honest readout' and one of the four columns of the detection-floor table. Substituting a median changes the statistic's efficiency and its detection floor (a median over 58 vertices has ~1.57x the variance of a mean under Gaussian noise), so the published floor for raw_roi_mean would be ~25% too high with no test failing. The additive-gain test cannot catch it because a median is equivariant under additive shifts.
findings.fix: Add a three-line value test: `g = np.arange(10.0); assert raw_roi_mean(g[None, :], np.array([0, 1, 9])) == pytest.approx((0 + 1 + 9) / 3)` — a case where the mean (3.333) and median (1.0) differ. Add the 1D-input path and the empty-ROI raise while there.

findings.title: The synthetic brain is duplicated from compositional_demo.py rather than imported — currently equivalent, but nothing prevents drift
findings.claim: The test file reimplements `build_brain` and `clip_map` from `scripts/compositional_demo.py` by hand. I verified the two are numerically identical TODAY, so the test does pin the same artifact the demo demonstrates — this is a latent risk, not a present error. But `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` already imports `build_brain, clip_map` from the demo directly, so the demo is the live shared fixture and any edit to it will silently desynchronise the regression test from the artifact it claims to pin.
findings.evidence: Direct numeric comparison: `FFCr idx identical: True | REST identical: True | base identical: True`, and for matched drive and clip seed, `aud=0.3: test spatial_z=0.904261 demo spatial_z=0.904261 equal=True`, `aud=0.54: test spatial_z=0.690056 demo spatial_z=0.690056 equal=True`. Two structural differences that are currently inert: the demo nests `A1 = idx['AUD'][:70]` inside the auditory mass and the test omits A1 entirely (the test never uses A1); and the demo returns `np.repeat(g[None, :], 11, axis=0)` while the test returns `g[None, :]` (all 11 rows are identical, so the `preds.mean(axis=0)` in every statistic makes them equal). The demo's `build_brain` also draws from a module-level `RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)` that is never reseeded, so it produces a different base on every call after the first — only the first call matches the test's `default_rng(0)`.
findings.concrete_failure: Change the demo's auditory baseline from 1.00 to 0.90 to better match a real prediction cache. `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` picks the change up automatically and recomputes the paper's floors under the new brain; `test_spatial_z_inverts_a_real_effect` keeps testing the old brain and keeps passing, so the regression test and the published floor table now describe two different worlds and nothing reports the divergence. Given the flagship test already sits within 0.056 of a sign flip (see the flagship finding), a modest change to the demo's mass structure could also make the artifact vanish in the table while the test still asserts it is present.
findings.fix: Import the fixture instead of copying it: `from scripts.compositional_demo import build_brain, clip_map` — `detection_floor_table.py` already proves this import path works. If the test must stay independent of `scripts/`, move the synthetic brain into `tribe_tools/` (or a `tests/fixtures.py`) and have both the demo and the tests import it, then add an equivalence test asserting the demo's `build_brain(seed=0)` base array equals the test fixture's to 1e-12 so any future drift fails loudly.

lanes.lane_summary: I read the full audited surface (`tribe_tools/roi_stats.py` lines 181-462 plus the rewritten `spatial_z` docstring, the 11 new tests, `scripts/detection_floor_table.py`), the ground-truth documents (`scripts/compositional_demo.py`, D025/D026/D027, G020-G024, M001-M007, MASTER-PLAN S1/S2/S3, `ops/source-of-truth.md`, `ops/interface-contracts.md`, `data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md` and `lookahead_scope.md`), and Meta's `predict()` in `/home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribev2-source/tribev2/demo_utils.py`. I ran the test suite (26 passed, 3.9 s), ran `compositional_demo.py` end to end, smoke-ran `detection_floor_table.py` (it does execute; ~1.53 s/experiment), and ran three targeted counter-experiments: (a) the floor table at the confound level it hard-codes (d_aud=0.24) versus no confound (d_aud=0.0); (b) a swap of the two hand-chosen ROI baseline drive constants; (c) seed-sensitivity and exact-vs-Monte-Carlo behaviour of `detection_floor`. The code is clean and the arithmetic is correct — I found no numerical error in any statistic. The paper is nevertheless rejectable on methods, and the reason is uniform: every load-bearing quantitative claim is a property of a synthetic brain whose free parameters were chosen to produce the claim, and the three counter-experiments make that demonstrable rather than rhetorical. Specifically: the three recommended replacements' power curves are bit-identical whether the injected confound is 0.00 or 0.24, so the synthetic brain contains exactly one nuisance channel and it is analytically invisible to all three replacements; `spatial_z` recovers a 0.05 effect at 93% power once that one channel is removed, so its "floor > 0.30" is a measurement of the injected bias, not of its sensitivity; and swapping the two stipulated baseline drive constants for FFCr and EBA exactly swaps the simulated ROI ordering, so "ordering exact" — the demonstration's headline evidence — is a restatement of an unmeasured input. Separately, `event_locked_response` contains a real, shippable bug that will silently corrupt S2: it indexes `preds` rows as if they were absolute TRs, but TRIBE's `predict()` returns only kept segments. Two claims I could not verify and flag as gaps rather than findings: what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports (not in `source-of-truth.md`, no paper text in the repo, no network), and whether Gate 0 loaded TRIBE v2 or v1 (G024 is still OPEN and is a live confound for the paper's "same pipeline" narrative).
lanes.search_failures: None. Every command completed cleanly and no search was killed or truncated. All greps were scoped to a single named file or directory with `--include`-equivalent narrowing, and no recursive search was run. Two verification gaps that are NOT search failures and must not be read as null results: (1) I could not verify the docstring claim that `glm_contrast_z` is "what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports" — the claim appears nowhere in `ops/source-of-truth.md`, the arXiv 2605.04326 text is not in the repo, and I have no network access; (2) I could not verify which checkpoint Gate 0 loaded (G024), for the same reason. Both are reported as findings requiring the authors to close them, not as things I searched for and failed to find.

findings.title: The demonstration's headline evidence ("ordering exact") is a restatement of an unmeasured input, not a prediction
findings.claim: The claim quoted in D026 and in the `spatial_z` docstring — that the zero-face simulation reproduces the observed FFCr/EBA/V1 ordering exactly — has zero evidential weight, because the ordering is determined entirely by three baseline drive constants the authors chose by hand and did not measure from anything. Under an sd-shift, Δz ≈ −z·(Δsd/sd), so the ordering of the simulated deltas is forced to follow the ordering of the stipulated baselines. A reviewer will read this as fitting four free parameters (three baselines plus the confound magnitude) to four observed numbers and then reporting the fit as a mechanism.
findings.evidence: `build_brain()` stipulates, with no cited source: `base[idx["V1"]] = 0.42`, `base[idx["FFCr"]] = 0.62`, `base[idx["EBA"]] = 0.72`. I swapped only the FFCr and EBA constants (0.62↔0.72) and re-ran `run(0.24)` unchanged: as shipped, `V1 d=-0.111 (zbase 0.254) FFCr d=-0.217 (zbase 0.815) EBA d=-0.267 (zbase 1.083)`; with the two constants swapped, `V1 d=-0.111 (zbase 0.255) FFCr d=-0.270 (zbase 1.093) EBA d=-0.215 (zbase 0.808)`. The simulated ordering inverts exactly with the stipulated input.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper's worked example asserts a mechanism for the retracted 2026-07-31 NO-GO. A reviewer sets FFCr's baseline drive above EBA's and the simulation now 'reproduces' the opposite ordering with equal fidelity. The mechanistic claim — 'the observed pattern is the sd-shift signature' — therefore survives no falsification test as written, and any conclusion drawn from it about real TRIBE predictions is unsupported.
findings.fix: The baseline spatial z of each ROI is directly measurable and is the demonstration's only real degree of freedom: report `spatial_z(grand-mean map, ROI)` for A1/V1/FFCr/EBA from the actual prediction cache and use those measured values as `build_brain`'s inputs instead of 0.42/0.62/0.72. Then 'ordering exact' becomes a genuine out-of-sample prediction. Until that is done, delete 'ordering exact' from every claim and state that the ordering is an assumed input.

findings.title: The synthetic brain contains exactly one nuisance channel, and it is analytically invisible to all three recommended replacements
findings.claim: `clip_map` scales only the AUD block and explicitly makes the per-clip global gain condition-independent, so the single injected confound cannot touch `raw_roi_mean`, `roi_minus_reference` or `glm_contrast_z` by construction. The comparison that motivates D027 is therefore not a comparison of statistics under a shared perturbation; it is a comparison of one statistic that is exposed to the only confound present against three that are analytically orthogonal to it. This is the definition of a rigged demonstration and it is the first thing a hostile reviewer will look for.
findings.evidence: `clip_map` body: `g[idx["AUD"]] *= 1.0 + aud_drive` (only AUD touched); `g += rng.normal(0, 0.05, N_VERTS)` and `g *= 1.0 + rng.normal(0, 0.04)` with the comment `# per-clip global gain, condition-independent`. I ran the floor computation at two confound levels (N_SIM=30, N_PERM=200, alpha=0.025). Power at effect 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 — d_aud=0.24: raw 0.47/1.00/1.00, ref 0.80/1.00/1.00, glm 0.50/1.00/1.00, spatial_z 0.00/0.00/0.10. d_aud=0.00: raw 0.47/1.00/1.00, ref 0.80/1.00/1.00, glm 0.50/1.00/1.00, spatial_z 0.40/0.93/1.00. The three replacement columns are bit-identical across a 0.24 change in the confound; only `spatial_z` moves.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper will claim the replacement statistics are robust where the compositional one fails. The evidence offered establishes only that a confound placed in a region none of the three statistics reads cannot move them. Add the one confound that is at least as plausible in real data — a condition-correlated global gain, i.e. FACE clips being 'louder everywhere' because they carry 18% more speech — and `raw_roi_mean` inherits it in full while `spatial_z` is the statistic that removes it. The recommendation to demote `spatial_z` in favour of `raw_roi_mean` is unsupported by this simulation and may be backwards for that nuisance.
findings.fix: Add at least two more nuisance channels to `clip_map`, each switchable and each condition-correlated: (a) a global additive/multiplicative gain whose magnitude differs between conditions, and (b) non-zero auditory-correlated drive inside the pre-registered reference region. Report the full statistic × nuisance-channel matrix. The paper's recommendation must be conditional on which nuisances are present, and the code should say which nuisance each statistic is and is not robust to.

findings.title: Detection floors are computed at exactly one confound level — the one tuned to reproduce the retracted result — so they measure bias, not sensitivity
findings.claim: `D_AUD = 0.24` is a module constant used by every cell of the table, and it was selected because it best reproduces the 2026-07-31 pattern. Under a one-sided FACE>NONFACE test, `spatial_z` at that confound level is strongly negatively biased, so its 'floor' is a measurement of the injected bias rather than of its detection sensitivity. The table's central comparison is therefore circular for the paper's central claim, and D027's own pre-registered revisit condition cannot be evaluated from it.
findings.evidence: `D_AUD = 0.24        # best match to the observed 2026-07-31 pattern`, used unconditionally inside `one_experiment`. Measured (N_SIM=30, N_PERM=200): at d_aud=0.24 `spatial_z` power is 0.00 at effect 0.05 and 0.10 at effect 0.10, so `interpolate_floor` will report '> 0.30 (never reached)'. At d_aud=0.00 the same statistic reaches 0.93 power at effect 0.05 and 1.00 at 0.10 — an implied floor near 0.03, roughly an order of magnitude below the number the table will print. D027 records the revisit condition 'the floor estimator shows the new statistics are less sensitive than spatial_z on a design where ground truth is known (it should be the reverse)'; with only one confound level in the script, that condition is untestable.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper publishes a design-requirements table stating that `spatial_z` cannot detect an effect below 0.30 while the replacements detect 0.02. A reviewer reruns the same script with `D_AUD = 0.0` and gets `spatial_z` detecting 0.05 at 93% power. The table's headline number is off by ~10× and its qualitative ranking of statistics reverses in the no-confound regime, which is the regime the table is implicitly claimed to describe ('a property of the DESIGN').
findings.fix: Make the confound magnitude an explicit axis of the floor table (at minimum d_aud ∈ {0.00, 0.12, 0.24}) and label every floor with the nuisance regime it was computed in. State plainly in the caption that `spatial_z`'s floor at d_aud>0 is a bias measurement, not a sensitivity measurement, and report its d_aud=0 floor beside it. This also discharges D027's revisit condition, which is currently unevaluated.

findings.title: event_locked_response indexes kept-segment rows as if they were absolute TRs; TRIBE's predict() drops empty segments
findings.claim: The function computes `rows = onsets_tr + lag_trs` and reads `p[rows]`, treating row index as absolute TR index. TRIBE v2's `predict()` returns `(n_kept_segments, n_vertices)` with empty segments discarded, and the mapping from row to time lives in the discarded `all_segments` return value, which this function neither accepts nor consults. The `IndexError` guard fires only when a read runs off the END of the array; it cannot detect misalignment, so a wrong read is silent — precisely the M001/silent-failure class the docstring claims to guard against.
findings.evidence: Code: `rows = np.asarray(list(onsets_tr), dtype=int) + int(lag_trs)` then `return p[rows][:, verts].mean(axis=1)`, with the parameter documented as `preds: (n_trs, n_vertices)`. Meta's `predict()` (/home/deveshb/workspace/AI/tribev2-source/tribev2/demo_utils.py): `keep = np.array([len(s.ns_events) > 0 for s in batch_segments])` … `y_pred = rearrange(y_pred, "b d t -> (b t) d")[keep]`, returning `preds, all_segments`. `ops/source-of-truth.md` marks VERIFIED: 'Dataloader window = duration_trs x TR = 100 s regardless of clip length' and 'A 10 s clip therefore yields ~11 rows of a 100 s window'. CLAUDE.md's memorized shapes state 'n_kept_segments ≠ n_total_segments — empty segments are dropped'.
findings.concrete_failure: S2's planned flashed-image localizer is 1 s on / 8 s ISI. If the events DataFrame carries one video event per 1-s image presentation — the natural way to build a flashed localizer — the ISI seconds contain no events and are dropped, so `preds` has one row per presentation, not one per second. With 50 exemplars and onsets [0, 9, 18, …], `event_locked_response(preds, verts, [0], lag_trs=5)` returns row 5, which is the sixth image's own onset second (true time t=45 s), not the HRF peak of image 1. Every event except the last five is silently misread as a different category's stimulus onset; the last five raise IndexError. The resulting FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA 'recovery' — the paper's second pillar — would be measured on the wrong timepoints.
findings.fix: Change the signature to take the time base explicitly: `event_locked_response(preds, segments_or_offsets, verts, onsets_s, lag_s=5.0)`. Build a row→offset map from `all_segments`, look up `onset_s + lag_s` in it, and raise loudly if that offset was dropped rather than falling through to positional indexing. Update `ops/interface-contracts.md` per CLAUDE.md rule 2. Add a regression test in which a middle segment is dropped and assert the function raises rather than returning a shifted read.

findings.title: Events sharing a 100 s bidirectional window are not exchangeable, so every per-event permutation null and every detection floor is anti-conservative
findings.claim: `event_locked_contrast` and the `perm_p`/`detection_floor` machinery treat individual events as independent, exchangeable observations. TRIBE v2's encoder is maskless and bidirectional over a 100-TR window, so the prediction at every timepoint is a function of the whole window, including stimuli presented AFTER it. At 1 s on / 8 s ISI, ~11 events share each window and are mutually dependent; furthermore each event's read sits at a different within-window position and therefore has a different amount of future context, which is an uncontrolled covariate of response magnitude.
findings.evidence: This repo's own verified findings: `data/algonauts/position_embed_dead.md` — 'config.yaml: causal:false → neuraltrain/models/transformer.py:69-72 returns Encoder, not Decoder'; 'Maskless attention means the representation at output position p is a function of all window positions, including everything after p'. `data/algonauts/lookahead_scope.md` — 'the prediction for within-window TR p attends over the whole ~100-TR window, including the (99−p) TRs after p'. `ops/source-of-truth.md` VERIFIED: 'Dataloader window = duration_trs x TR = 100 s regardless of clip length'. Neither `event_locked_contrast` nor `detection_floor` has any window or block parameter; `detection_floor`'s model is `rng.normal(effect, noise_sd, n_per_group)` — i.i.d. by construction.
findings.concrete_failure: With m≈11 events per 100 s window and intra-window correlation ρ, the effective sample size is n/(1+(m−1)ρ). At ρ=0.3 the design effect is 4.0, so a permutation p-value computed over 50 nominally independent face exemplars is calibrated as if there were ~12, and `detection_floor(n_per_group=50, …)` understates the true MDE by roughly a factor of 2. A category recovered at p=0.01 could be at p>0.1 under a window-blocked null. If exemplars are presented in category blocks, category is additionally confounded with within-window position and hence with amount of future context, so the contrast is partly a lookahead effect.
findings.fix: Either present one exemplar per forward pass (each event gets its own 100 s window, restoring independence at real GPU cost), or permute at the WINDOW level rather than the event level and report the cluster-robust p. Record the exemplar-to-window assignment and the within-window position of every read, randomize category order across windows and positions, and report response magnitude against within-window position as a diagnostic. Add the window/block structure as an explicit parameter of `detection_floor` and report the design effect.

findings.title: The headline statistic-comparison table is a single unreplicated realization with frozen seeds
findings.claim: The 'THE DECISION-RELEVANT CASE' table — the numbers quoted verbatim in the `spatial_z` docstring, in D026 reasoning point 3, and pinned by `test_spatial_z_inverts_a_real_effect` — is one draw. `clip_map` is called with fixed seeds `1000+i` and `2000+i` in every row of every table, so the per-clip noise realization never changes, and the injected effect is added AFTER the multiplicative gain so it enters noise-free. There is no repetition, no sampling distribution, no Type-I check, and no error bar behind any published number.
findings.evidence: `run()` calls `clip_map(base, idx, a_f, seed=1000 + i)` and `clip_map(base, idx, a_n, seed=2000 + i)` — fixed across all invocations; the effect is applied afterwards as `pf[:, idx["FFCr"]] += face_effect`. My run of the shipped script shows the consequence exactly: FFCr `raw d` is constant at −0.0054/−0.0055 across every row of the d_aud sweep (0.00 through 0.18), and in the effect table it is deterministically `effect − 0.0055`: 0.02→+0.0146, 0.05→+0.0446, 0.10→+0.0946, 0.20→+0.1946, 0.40→+0.3945. The quoted 'p=0.0005' is the estimator floor 1/(2000+1), i.e. zero of 2000 permutations, not a measured value.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper reports 'raw and reference statistics detect a genuine 0.05 effect at p=0.0005 while spatial_z reports p=0.9985'. Whether the null offset is −0.0055 or +0.02 is pure luck of seeds 1000-1014 versus 2000-2014, and it is never resampled. A reviewer reruns with different clip seeds and gets a different table. Worse, because the effect bypasses the per-clip gain, raw's detection is noise-free by construction, so p collapses to the estimator floor for reasons that will not hold in real data.
findings.fix: Wrap the whole comparison in ≥1000 independent replications with resampled clip seeds; report median and 5-95% interval for every cell, plus the empirical Type-I rate at effect 0 for each statistic. Inject the effect BEFORE the global gain so it carries the same nuisance as the signal. Report 'p < 5e-4' rather than 'p = 0.0005' anywhere the Monte-Carlo floor is hit, and state n_perm beside it.

findings.title: The reproduction claim omits the one ROI that carries the posited mechanism, and that ROI accounts for 83% of the fit error
findings.claim: The docstring and D026 both summarize the simulation by quoting FFCr (sim −0.239 vs obs −0.244) and, in D026, EBA and V1 — but silently drop A1. A1 is the ROI the posited mechanism acts on directly: the entire story is that FACE clips drove more auditory mass. The simulation misses A1 by more than an order of magnitude, and that single ROI supplies 83% of the reported sum-of-squares error. The mechanism fails on its own diagnostic.
findings.evidence: Shipped script output at the best-fit setting: `A1 sim d=+0.020 obs d=+0.280`, `V1 −0.124 / −0.046`, `FFCr −0.239 / −0.244`, `EBA −0.295 / −0.382`, total sum-sq error 0.0810. Per-ROI contributions: A1 (0.020−0.280)²=0.0676 (83.2%), EBA 0.00757, V1 0.00608, FFCr 0.000025. The `spatial_z` docstring quotes only 'FFCr sim -0.239 vs obs -0.244, ordering exact'; D026 reasoning point 3 lists FFCr, EBA and V1 and omits A1 entirely.
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer computes the per-ROI residuals and finds that the single number the paper reports (FFCr) is the best-fitting of four by a factor of 240 in squared error, while the ROI whose behaviour is the causal claim is off by 14×. The natural reading is that the simulation reproduces the three ROIs it was parameterised to reproduce and fails the one that would falsify it, and that the write-up quotes only the former.
findings.fix: Report all four ROIs with residuals and the per-ROI error contribution in the docstring, in D026, and in the paper. State explicitly that the simulation does not reproduce A1's observed +0.280 and explain why (in the simulation the sd rises in step with A1's mean, holding its z flat). Treat A1 as the falsification test the mechanism must pass, not as an omitted row.

findings.title: The two statistics D027 designates as PRIMARY ship with no inference procedure and no detection floor
findings.claim: D027 makes `event_locked_contrast` the primary statistic and adds `glm_contrast_z`, and requires under D-3 that 'every verdict carries a detection floor'. Both return a single scalar with no null distribution, and `detection_floor`'s model — two independent groups of per-observation scalars with additive Gaussian noise — cannot be applied to either. The module therefore ships a doctrine that its own API cannot satisfy for the statistics it promotes.
findings.evidence: `event_locked_contrast` returns `float(tgt.mean() - np.mean([o.mean() for o in others]))` — one scalar, no variance, no p. `glm_contrast_z` returns `float(z.mean())` — one scalar. `detection_floor`'s `achieved_power` is hard-wired to `a = rng.normal(effect, noise_sd, n_per_group); b = rng.normal(0.0, noise_sd, n_per_group); mc_perm_p(a, b, …)`. `scripts/detection_floor_table.py` had to hand-roll a bespoke permutation for `glm_contrast_z` (`pool = np.concatenate([fa, fb]); … glm_contrast_z(pool[perm[:N]], pool[perm[N:]], ffc) >= obs`) because no shipped helper exists, and no floor helper exists for `event_locked_contrast` at all.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 computes `event_locked_contrast` for FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA and must report a verdict plus a floor for each. There is no shipped way to obtain either a p-value or a floor for that statistic, so the analyst will either invent one ad hoc (unreviewed, unversioned, exactly how `spatial_z` became the primary in the first place) or report a bare effect size — which is the D-3 violation the paper is written to condemn.
findings.fix: Ship `event_locked_perm_p` (permute category labels at the WINDOW level, per the exchangeability finding) and `glm_contrast_perm_p`, promote the hand-rolled permutation out of the script into `roi_stats.py`, and generalise `detection_floor` to take a callable statistic plus a callable data generator so a floor can be produced for any of the four statistics. Add `ops/interface-contracts.md` entries for all of them.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z contradicts the spec in D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1, cites an unverified fact about Meta's Fig 4, and its non-compositionality test cannot fail
findings.claim: Three problems in one function. (1) Both D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1 specify 'effect/SE across time per vertex'; the implementation computes effect/SE across OBSERVATIONS, and `detection_floor_table.py` averages time away entirely before calling it. (2) The docstring asserts 'What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports' — a fact about the model's own paper that is absent from `ops/source-of-truth.md`, which CLAUDE.md rule 1 and M006 both forbid. (3) The test offered as evidence of non-compositionality is a tautology.
findings.evidence: MASTER-PLAN S1: '`glm_contrast_z` (effect/SE across time per vertex — non-compositional, and what Meta's Fig 4 actually reports)'. D027: 'a GLM contrast z (effect/SE across time per vertex — what the paper's Fig 4 reports)'. Implementation: `av, bv = a[:, verts], b[:, verts]; diff = av.mean(axis=0) - bv.mean(axis=0); var = ((na-1)*av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) + (nb-1)*bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1))/(na+nb-2)` with docstring 'across observations'. `detection_floor_table.py` feeds it `fa = np.array([p.mean(axis=0) for p in face])` — time collapsed first. `grep -c roi_stats ops/interface-contracts.md` returns 0. The test: `a2[:, 200:] += 9.0` then `assert abs(before - after) < 1e-9` — but the function only ever reads `a[:, verts]` with `verts = np.arange(0,50)`, so columns 200+ are unread and the assertion holds by array indexing regardless of the statistic's properties.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper claims its GLM z matches the published one. If Meta's Fig 4 is a within-run temporal GLM (effect/SE over TRs with an HRF-convolved regressor, df ≈ n_TRs) and this is a between-clip two-sample z (df = na+nb−2 = 28 at n=15), the two differ in estimator, in degrees of freedom, and in what variance component they treat as noise — a referee who knows Fig 4 rejects on that sentence alone. Meanwhile `test_glm_contrast_z_is_unmoved_by_a_distant_region` would pass unchanged if `glm_contrast_z` were replaced by `lambda a,b,v: 0.0`.
findings.fix: Read arXiv 2605.04326 and record the exact Fig 4 estimator in `ops/source-of-truth.md` with a line citation before any claim of correspondence survives; if it is a temporal GLM, either implement that or amend D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1 to say what was actually built and why. Replace the vacuous test with one that perturbs the ROI's OWN vertices — e.g. a condition-correlated multiplicative gain applied brain-wide including the ROI — and assert the documented behaviour. Add all seven new functions to `ops/interface-contracts.md` (CLAUDE.md rule 2).

findings.title: The demonstration's one falsifiable prediction is untestable because the prediction cache it targets no longer exists
findings.claim: The script prints the normaliser shift under the heading 'THE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION FOR THE REAL CACHE'. That prediction has never been tested, and the repo's own records say the data required to test it was lost. This is the single missing control that decides whether the paper's worked example is about TRIBE or about a simulation the authors wrote.
findings.evidence: Script output: `brain_mean FACE 0.33924 NONFACE 0.31576 p=0.0005`, `brain_sd FACE 0.40844 NONFACE 0.33370 p=0.0005 ratio 1.2240`. `ops/knowledge-gaps.md` G020: 'Status: OPEN — needs the HDF5 prediction cache from the 2026-07-31 Kaggle session', with the closing tests specified as '(a) test g.mean() and g.std() FACE vs NONFACE; (b) recompute FFC z against a reference mask excluding auditory+STS'. D028: 'Kaggle /kaggle/working is lost on interactive session end unless Persistence was enabled beforehand — which is how ~4 GPU-hours went missing on 07-31.'
findings.concrete_failure: The paper claims the 2026-07-31 NO-GO was a normaliser artifact and offers a synthetic reproduction as proof. The prediction that would confirm it on real data — brain_sd is ~22% larger for FACE clips than NONFACE clips — is stated but never checked, and cannot be checked from any surviving artifact. If the real sd_ratio is 1.02 rather than 1.22, the sd-shift mechanism is 10× too small to produce the observed −0.244 and the paper's central explanation is wrong. As written, the reviewer cannot distinguish 'we proved the artifact' from 'we constructed a simulation that resembles our result'.
findings.fix: This is the single control whose absence should kill the paper: re-run the 30 clips (≈1.5 h T4 per the S2 budget, and the bank is required anyway under D028) and report, on real predictions, (a) g.mean() and g.std() FACE vs NONFACE with the permutation p, (b) FFCr renormalised against a reference excluding auditory+STS, (c) FFCr−EBA per clip. Two of the four numbers are already specified in G020. Without them the synthetic demonstration must be framed as a hypothesis about the retracted result, never as its explanation.

findings.title: G024 is open: the 'confident wrong answer' and the 'same pipeline recovering FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA' may not be the same model
findings.claim: The paper's structure is 'here is our confident wrong answer, and here is the SAME pipeline recovering the regions once the published protocol is used'. It is not established that the wrong answer came from the same model the replication will use. If Gate 0 loaded TRIBE v1, the comparison confounds a statistic change with a model change, and the in-silico localizer claim being replicated does not exist for the model that produced the null.
findings.evidence: `ops/knowledge-gaps.md` G024: 'the in-silico localizer result exists only for v2 (facebook/tribev2). If any run loaded v1 weights from facebookresearch/algonauts-2025, its interpretation changes entirely. The 07-31 results JSON records the tribev2 commit af58661791a351a448a489042a28f6c37e1c14b7 but the tribe-bench clone FAILED that session and no tribe-bench SHA was recorded. … Status: OPEN.' MASTER-PLAN S2 carries the same warning as a checklist item: '⚠ Confirm which checkpoint Gate 0 actually loaded'. G022: 'TRIBE v1 (arXiv 2507.22229, facebookresearch/algonauts-2025) is a DIFFERENT, earlier model'.
findings.concrete_failure: A referee asks which checkpoint produced the −0.244 and which will produce the recovery. If the answer is v1 then v2, the before/after figure varies two things at once and the paper's causal claim about the statistic is unsupported. G024 is flagged in the repo as 'cheap to close', which makes leaving it open before submission indefensible rather than merely unlucky.
findings.fix: Close G024 before writing: check the `from_pretrained` argument in the Gate 0 notebook and in `tribe_tools/model.py:load_model` against the HF model card, and record the checkpoint revision hash in `ops/source-of-truth.md`. Every figure caption must name the checkpoint. If the two arms used different checkpoints, either re-run the worked example on v2 or reframe the paper so the model change is the stated variable.

findings.title: detection_floor reports a single-seed point estimate with no uncertainty, and simulates a different test than the verdict runs at small n
findings.claim: Three defects in a number destined for a published table. (1) `achieved_power` re-seeds with the same `seed` on every call, so the returned MDE is conditional on one fixed set of n_sim draws and carries no reported uncertainty. (2) It calls `mc_perm_p` unconditionally, whereas the verdict path `perm_p` enumerates exactly when C(N,n) ≤ 20000, i.e. for n_per_group ≤ 8 — so at small n the floor describes a test the verdict does not run, contradicting the docstring's 'the same one-sided permutation test the verdict uses'. (3) The docstring's 'It is a property of the DESIGN … not of any observed data' is false whenever `noise_sd` is estimated from the same clips that produced the verdict, and no estimator is shipped to do it any other way.
findings.evidence: Code: `def achieved_power(effect): rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)` — same seed each call; `if mc_perm_p(a, b, n_perm=n_perm, seed=…)`. `perm_p`: `if comb(N, n) <= 20000: return exact_perm_p(...)`. Measured: `detection_floor(15, noise_sd=1.0, n_sim=60, n_perm=200, tol=0.02)` over seeds 0-4 gives [1.125, 1.094, 1.219, 1.172, 1.125] — a spread of 0.125, 10.9% of the mean. At n=8 with a true effect of 0.9 sd, rejection rate at alpha=0.025 is 0.303 under `exact_perm_p` versus 0.283 under `mc_perm_p(n_perm=400)` (300 replications), a 7% relative power difference; minimum achievable p is 8e-5 exact versus 2.5e-3 Monte-Carlo.
findings.concrete_failure: The paper prints 'MDE = 1.12' in a design-requirements table. Re-running with seed=2 gives 1.22. For a small-n row (n=6 or 8), the tabulated floor is systematically wrong because the verdict would have used exact enumeration with far finer p-value granularity. And an analyst who plugs the observed sample sd of a null result into `noise_sd` gets a floor contaminated by any real effect present in those very data.
findings.fix: Report the MDE as an interval: resample the simulation seed R times and print the median with a 5-95% range, or bootstrap the bisection. Route through `perm_p` rather than `mc_perm_p` so the simulated test matches the verdict's test exactly. Amend the docstring to state that the floor is conditional on the supplied `noise_sd`, and ship an explicit estimator (e.g. from held-out or negative-control clips) so the noise input is not silently taken from the test data.

findings.title: interpolate_floor reports an already-powered design as 'never reached', inverting the conclusion; the script's stated runtime is ~10x optimistic
findings.claim: `interpolate_floor` scans from i=1 for the first index satisfying `powers[i] >= target > powers[i-1]`. If the design is already at or above target power at the smallest effect in the grid (including effect 0.0), no index can satisfy the strict `target > powers[i-1]` clause, the function returns None, and `main` prints '> 0.30 (never reached)' — the exact opposite of the truth. Separately, the module docstring claims '~2-4 minutes' for a script that has never been successfully executed.
findings.evidence: Code: `for i in range(1, len(effects)): if powers[i] >= target > powers[i-1]: …` then `return None`; `main` renders None as `f"> {EFFECTS[-1]:.2f} (never reached)"`. Direct check: `interpolate_floor((0.0, 0.1), (0.9, 0.95))` returns `None`. Measured runtime of `one_experiment` at shipped settings: 1.53 s; the script runs 11 effects x 100 sims = 1100 experiments ≈ 28 minutes, against the docstring's '~2-4 minutes'. The file header states it has never been run.
findings.concrete_failure: If a future design is well powered even at the smallest grid effect — which is the intended outcome once n rises to the S3 target of ≥40 per condition — the table prints 'floor > 0.30 (not reached)' for a statistic whose true floor is below 0.005, and the paper concludes the design is insensitive when it is in fact excellent. The runtime error is minor but means the table has not been produced, so no floor currently exists to publish.
findings.fix: Return 0.0 (or `effects[0]`, flagged '≤ smallest grid point') when `powers[0] >= target`, and return None only when the target is never reached at the largest effect. Since Monte-Carlo power curves are non-monotone, fit a monotone curve or take the LAST crossing rather than the first. Correct the runtime estimate, run the script, and commit `data/floor_table_v3b.md`.

findings.title: define_froi cannot enforce the independence it depends on and selects by raw mean difference, so it manufactures a selective ROI from pure noise
findings.claim: D027 and MASTER-PLAN S1 present `define_froi` as the fix for the ROI, but the function's only defence against double dipping is a prose warning. Its signature accepts any two arrays, so passing the test data itself is a silent, single-character-cheap mistake. It also selects by the unnormalised mean difference `a[pv] - b[pv]` with no threshold and no statistical criterion, so it always returns exactly `top_n` vertices, ranked, even when both inputs are pure noise.
findings.evidence: Code: `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]; keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]`, preceded only by a `.. warning::` docstring that 'loc_a / loc_b MUST come from a held-out localizer run'. When 2D input is supplied the function does `a = a.mean(axis=0) if a.ndim == 2 else a`, discarding the per-vertex variance, so vertices are ranked by mean difference rather than by a t or z. The tests exercise only the noiseless case (`a[np.arange(150,160)] = 1.0`, everything else exactly 0) and the parcel-size cap; no test covers the noise-only case or the double-dipping case.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 defines the face fROI from half the exemplars and tests on the other half. If a future caller passes the full set to both `define_froi` and the contrast — which the signature permits and nothing detects — the fROI is the 100 most face-selective vertices of the test data itself and the subsequent p-value is meaningless. Even used correctly, ranking by unnormalised difference preferentially selects high-variance vertices, so the fROI is partly a noise-magnitude map.
findings.fix: Change the signature to take the full data plus explicit disjoint index sets (`localizer_idx`, `test_idx`) and assert they do not intersect, so independence is structurally enforced rather than requested; or ship a `split_half` helper and make it the documented entry point. Rank by a per-vertex t/z rather than the raw difference. Add two tests: pure noise in both conditions must not yield a fROI that survives a split-half check, and overlapping localizer/test indices must raise.

findings.title: With S2 and S3 not started, the paper's remaining contribution is a synthetic worked example of a known artifact
findings.claim: The paper's three-part claim is (1) the compositional statistic inverts real effects, (2) the same pipeline recovers FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA under the published protocol, (3) therefore a design-requirements table with detection floors. Part 1 is explicitly disclaimed as non-novel by the project's own decision log. Parts 2 and 3 do not exist. What remains is a synthetic demonstration of global signal regression plus a self-report.
findings.evidence: D027: 'This is not a new discovery — it is the global-signal-regression artifact (Murphy et al. 2009) and, in the interpretability setting, arXiv 2512.18792 ("The Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability", Méloux et al.). **Do not write it up as a novel methods contribution.**' MASTER-PLAN: 'S2 — The replication … STATUS: not started'; 'S3 — Design requirements … blocked by S2'. S2 additionally carries a blocking gate that has already failed once: 'Our v3b run got A1 speech at p=0.1448 … If a contrast the literature says is near-ceiling still does not come out strongly positive, the pipeline is broken and nothing else in this plan means anything.' Deadline 2026-08-29 AoE.
findings.concrete_failure: A reviewer reads part 1, recognises Murphy 2009, and checks what is left. Parts 2 and 3 are synthetic: the floors come from a brain the authors wrote, at one confound level they tuned, in units the floor table's own caveat admits are uncalibrated ('the constant relating them to real TRIBE units is unverified until S2 produces real predictions'). The submission reduces to a retraction narrative with a simulation, which is a real ICBINB-BIO genre but a substantially weaker one than the abstract promises.
findings.fix: Either run S2 and report real recovered fROIs with real floors — including the speech→auditory blocking gate, whose failure is itself a legitimate result — or retitle the submission honestly as a retraction-and-diagnosis case study, drop the design-requirements table to an appendix explicitly labelled synthetic, and lead with the one thing D029 identifies as unclaimed: the prediction bank. Do not present synthetic-unit floors as design requirements in the abstract.

lanes.lane_summary: MATHEMATICAL CORRECTNESS lane. I re-derived each new statistic from scratch and checked the implementation against my derivation, then ran numerical experiments to confirm or refute every concern the brief raised. WHAT IS CORRECT (negative results, stated so nobody re-litigates them): (a) glm_contrast_z's pooled SE is algebraically exact — it reproduces scipy.stats.ttest_ind(equal_var=True) to 2.2e-16 at na/nb = 5/5, 4/12, 12/4, 2/30, 15/15, so ddof and the (na-1)/(nb-1) weighting are right; (b) detection_floor is sound — achieved_power is empirically monotone under common random numbers (no violations on a 0.05 grid over effect 0.60-1.60), re-seeding with the same seed IS correct CRN because numpy's normal(loc,...) consumes the same stream regardless of loc, the doubling loop brackets [hi/2, hi] so it cannot overshoot, it cannot return 0, and the returned floor matches the exact noncentral-t MDE adjusted for the rank test's 0.955 ARE to 0.2% at n=15 (1.0830 vs 1.0845) and 1.5% at n=24; the +8% at n=6 is genuine permutation discreteness, not a bug; (c) using mc_perm_p(n_perm=400) inside detection_floor instead of the exact enumeration perm_p dispatches to at n=6 costs at most 1 percentage point of power, so the floor does describe the test the verdict uses; (d) mean-of-z vs z-of-ROI-mean — for a uniform effect under homoscedastic equicorrelated noise the two have identical SNR to first order (both delta*sqrt(n/2)/(sigma*sqrt(rho+(1-rho)/V))), and mean-of-z is strictly better under heteroscedastic per-vertex noise, so there is NO power pathology from correlation; (e) the ndim branch in raw_roi_mean/roi_minus_reference has no latent bug — 1D and 2D agree exactly (2.0/2.0 and -52.5/-52.5 on matched inputs), 3D and 0D raise IndexError, a list raises AttributeError, and the overlap guard fires; (f) event_locked_contrast's mean-of-category-means matches its docstring and is the unbiased estimator of the equal-weight baseline (higher variance than pooling only at unequal exemplar counts, which is the intended trade); (g) 26/26 tests pass. WHAT IS WRONG: seven defects, one of which I rate critical. The headline is that glm_contrast_z uses a POOLED (equal-variance) standard error. That is exactly right at equal n and provably wrong at unequal n: at the S2 design shape (faces n=50 vs pooled other categories n=200, V=58 vertices, rho=0.6, 800 replicates, n_perm=400) the permutation test's Type I error is correctly calibrated at 0.0225 when the two conditions have equal across-exemplar sd, but rises to 0.0650 (2.6x nominal, 4.6 SE) at a modest 1.5:1 sd ratio and 0.125 (5x) at 3:1, and collapses to 0.0050 and then exactly 0.0000 in the other direction — a guaranteed NO-GO no matter how large the true effect. Swapping in a Welch (unpooled) SE restores calibration to 0.033-0.038 across all four stress cases. Also: define_froi's argsort-reverse ranking puts NaN first, so a localizer with any non-finite vertex returns an fROI composed entirely of dead vertices (demonstrated exactly), and event_locked_response indexes rows as TRs while ops/source-of-truth.md:52,89 verifies the model returns (n_kept_segments, n_vertices) with empty segments dropped.
lanes.search_failures: Two Bash calls exceeded the 120 s foreground limit and were moved to background; both completed with exit code 0 and I read their full output (seed-sensitivity sweep of detection_floor, and the 800-replicate Type I baseline). No search or test was killed or truncated. One genuine failure to report: `np.load('data/algonauts/sub-01_ood_fmri_samples.npy', allow_pickle=False)` errored with "Object arrays cannot be loaded when allow_pickle=False", so I could NOT check the project's real arrays for NaN or zero-variance vertices. Findings 2 and 5 therefore demonstrate the NaN/zero-variance code paths on synthetic input only; I have not established how often TRIBE's actual predictions contain non-finite or constant vertices, and that premise should be checked against a real prediction cache before prioritising those two.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z uses a pooled (equal-variance) SE; at unequal n its permutation test is not level-alpha in either direction
findings.claim: The standard error is Student's POOLED two-sample SE, which assumes the two conditions have equal across-observation variance. That assumption is harmless at equal n (permutation tests are famously robust there) but fails badly at unequal n. Because the resulting statistic is not asymptotically pivotal, wrapping it in a permutation test does NOT rescue it (Behrens-Fisher; cf. Janssen 1997, Chung & Romano 2013 on studentised permutation tests). The MASTER-PLAN S2 design is faces (n>=50) versus the pooled other categories (n>=200) - unequal n by 1:4, with the pooled 'other' arm heterogeneous by construction - which is precisely the configuration that breaks.
findings.evidence: Line 339-340: `var = ((na - 1) * av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) + (nb - 1) * bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1)) / (na + nb - 2)` then `se = np.sqrt(var * (1.0 / na + 1.0 / nb))`. I confirmed this is exactly Student's pooled t, not Welch: it reproduces scipy.stats.ttest_ind(..., equal_var=True) to <=2.2e-16 at (na,nb) = (5,5), (4,12), (12,4), (2,30), (15,15). Measured Type I error of the permutation test on glm_contrast_z (the exact test used at scripts/detection_floor_table.py:76-83), na=50 vs nb=200, V=58, equicorrelated vertices rho=0.6, TRUE MEANS IDENTICAL, nominal one-sided alpha=0.025, n_perm=400, 800 replicates: sd_a/sd_b=1.00 -> 0.0225 +/- 0.0052 (calibrated); sd_a/sd_b=1.50 -> 0.0650 +/- 0.0087 (2.6x nominal, 4.6 SE above); sd_a/sd_b=0.67 -> 0.0050 +/- 0.0025 (5x deflated). Pushed harder (400 reps, n_perm=300): sd ratio 3:1 -> Type I 0.1250; ratio 1:3 -> Type I 0.0000, i.e. the test can never reject at any effect size. Equal n is immune: na=nb=15 with a 1:3 sd ratio gives Type I 0.0250. Replacing only the SE with Welch, se = sqrt(var_a/na + var_b/nb), restores calibration at 50v200 across all four stress cases: 0.0325, 0.0375, 0.0325, 0.0350.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 runs glm_contrast_z(faces_50xV, others_200xV, ffc_verts) and permutes it. Case A - faces are the more variable arm by 1.5x (plausible: fLoc face exemplars vary in viewpoint/identity while the pooled others average out): the test rejects a TRUE NULL 6.5% of the time at nominal 2.5%, and the paper publishes 'TRIBE has a face-selective FFA' off a false positive. Case B - the pooled four-category 'other' arm is the more variable one by 1.5x (the likelier case, since pooling heterogeneous categories inflates variance): Type I drops to 0.005 and at a 3:1 ratio to exactly 0.000, so the statistic reports NO-GO no matter how large the real face effect is. That is the same class of error as the retracted 2026-07-31 spatial_z result - a NO-GO manufactured by the normaliser rather than by the data - reached by a different route, in the statistic built to replace it.
findings.fix: Replace the pooled variance with a Welch (unpooled) SE: `se = np.sqrt(av.var(axis=0, ddof=1) / na + bv.var(axis=0, ddof=1) / nb)`, deleting the `var = ...` pooling line. This is the studentised-permutation form and is asymptotically pivotal, so the surrounding permutation test becomes approximately exact under heteroscedasticity; I verified it restores Type I to 0.033-0.038 at 50v200 for sd ratios 2:1 through 1:3. It is identical to the current code when na == nb and the variances match, so no existing test changes meaning. Additionally, add a test that pins Type I at unequal n with unequal variance, and update ops/interface-contracts.md per CLAUDE.md rule 2 (the signature is unchanged but the documented statistic is not).

findings.title: define_froi ranks with argsort()[::-1], which sorts NaN to the FRONT - a localizer with dead vertices returns an fROI made entirely of them
findings.claim: np.argsort puts NaN LAST in ascending order; reversing with [::-1] therefore puts NaN FIRST. Any non-finite value in the localizer contrast is treated as the most face-selective vertex in the parcel. There is no isfinite guard anywhere in the function. Separately, on a localizer with no signal at all (all selectivity values tied) the same line silently returns the highest-index vertices of the parcel rather than raising - so a broken or empty localizer still produces a confident-looking fROI.
findings.evidence: Line 387-389: `sel = a[pv] - b[pv]` then `keep = pv[np.argsort(sel)[::-1][:k]]`. Run: loc_a with ten genuinely selective vertices at indices 100-109 (value 1.0) and ten NaN vertices at 150-159, loc_b all zeros, parcel = arange(100,200), top_n=10. define_froi returns [150, 151, 152, 153, 154, 155, 156, 157, 158, 159] - the NaN vertices - and none of the ten real ones. Separately, define_froi(np.zeros(200), np.zeros(200), np.arange(100,200), top_n=8) returns [192, 193, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198, 199] with no error. The existing tests (test_define_froi_picks_the_selective_vertices, test_define_froi_caps_at_parcel_size) use only clean finite inputs and do not catch either case.
findings.concrete_failure: S2 defines the face fROI from half the localizer exemplars and tests on the other half. If the localizer half contains any vertex where TRIBE emitted NaN or where the medial-wall mask left non-finite values, the fROI becomes those dead vertices. The subsequent held-out contrast is then computed over vertices that carry no signal, returns a null, and the paper reports 'no face selectivity in a properly defined fROI' - a headline null caused entirely by a sort-order artifact, with the double-dipping safeguard in the docstring providing false reassurance that the ROI definition was done correctly.
findings.fix: Guard before ranking: `finite = np.isfinite(sel)`; if not finite.all(), either raise ValueError naming the offending vertex count or restrict pv/sel to the finite subset and reduce k accordingly (raise if fewer than top_n finite vertices remain). Also raise when the k-th and (k+1)-th selectivity values are exactly equal to the maximum-tie value across the whole parcel (a flat localizer), rather than returning an arbitrary index-ordered subset. Add both as tests.

findings.title: event_locked_response indexes prediction rows as if they were TRs, but predict() returns (n_kept_segments, n_vertices) with empty segments dropped
findings.claim: The function computes `rows = onsets_tr + lag_trs` and indexes `p[rows]` directly, treating row index as TR index. ops/source-of-truth.md verifies that TRIBE v2's predict() returns (n_kept_segments, n_vertices) and that segments with no events are removed by default, so row index and TR index differ by however many segments were dropped before that point. The only guard present is a bounds check; a misalignment leaves rows in range and is therefore completely silent - the exact silent-failure class the docstring says it is guarding against.
findings.evidence: Lines 268-276: `rows = np.asarray(list(onsets_tr), dtype=int) + int(lag_trs)` ... `if rows.min() < 0 or rows.max() >= p.shape[0]: raise IndexError(...)` ... `return p[rows][:, verts].mean(axis=1)`. Against ops/source-of-truth.md line 89 (`Segments with no events are removed by default (remove_empty_segments=True) | VERIFIED | demo_utils.py:148, 370-376`) and line 52 (`A 10 s clip therefore yields ~11 rows of a 100 s window => ~90% of the model window is exact zeros | VERIFIED`), which together establish that the returned array is compacted, not TR-indexed. CLAUDE.md's Data Shapes section repeats this: 'n_kept_segments != n_total_segments - empty segments are dropped'. TR = 1.0 s is verified (source-of-truth line 49), so lag_trs=5 really is 5 s - the lag arithmetic itself is right; only the row->TR identification is wrong. Confirmed by grep that there is currently no production caller (only tests/test_roi_stats.py:244,252), so this is latent, not yet biting.
findings.concrete_failure: S2's localizer is 1 s image on / 8 s ISI. If the blank ISI segments carry no Audio/Video events they are dropped, so a stimulus at true TR 90 (the 11th event) lands at row ~10 in the returned array. event_locked_response(preds, verts, onsets_tr=[0,9,18,...,90], lag_trs=5) reads row 95, which is either off the end (loud) or, for a longer run, a completely unrelated event (silent). Every category mean is then computed from the wrong events, event_locked_contrast returns noise, and the FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA replication - the paper's positive control against Meta's published result - fails for a reason that looks like a model failure and will be reported as one.
findings.fix: Do not accept a bare array. Either (a) take the `all_segments` list that predict() returns alongside preds and resolve each onset to its row via the segment start times, raising if an onset falls in a dropped segment; or (b) require the caller to pass an explicit `n_trs` and assert `preds.shape[0] == n_trs`, so a compacted array fails loudly instead of silently misaligning. Record the chosen contract in ops/interface-contracts.md before S2 is written.

findings.title: glm_contrast_z is documented and named as a z-score but its null SD ranges from 0.14 to 1.06 depending only on inter-vertex correlation
findings.claim: The ROI value is the arithmetic mean of V per-vertex t-statistics. Under the null its variance is approximately (rho_bar + (1 - rho_bar)/V) * df/(df-2), where rho_bar is the mean inter-vertex correlation of the noise - a nuisance parameter with nothing to do with the effect. The returned number is therefore not on the z scale and cannot be thresholded at 1.96, converted through the normal CDF, or compared numerically to the per-vertex z values in Meta's Fig 4, even though the docstring says it is 'What Meta's Fig 4 actually reports'.
